Ported the identical dedicated test to `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts` against the real generated `buildCalendarIcs`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `calendarIcs.ts` and `codegen.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to HEAD (keeping the updated tests). Both predicted failures occurred exactly: the ASCII fold test failed too (confirming the leading-space off-by-one is a general bug, not Hebrew-specific), and the Hebrew test failed with a 127-byte unfolded `DESCRIPTION` line reported as a single physical line -- the exact unfolded-Hebrew bug this round fixes, reproduced on demand. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **812 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/db` (**127**), `@forge/shared` (**16**), `@forge/spec-engine` (**93**) stayed at their round-426 counts. Pushed as commit `3f5e4ce`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed -- one of the long-standing "small open candidates" list's original entries (`calendarIcs.ts`'s UTF-16-vs-UTF-8 fold, carried since round 367) to finally get implemented. It also demonstrates the value of letting a fresh survey re-derive an already-known-but-deferred item rather than only hunting for brand-new ground: the item had been correctly identified as real back in round 367 but never prioritized, and writing a genuinely adversarial regression test for it (Hebrew content, every physical line checked) surfaced a second bug the original feature's own test suite had never caught either. Everything else still open from rounds 378-426 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 431: deleting a WhatsApp message could be silently undone by an in-flight background poll

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at round 430's own fresh lessons (byte-vs-character length checks elsewhere, Hebrew-fixture test gaps) and round 426's (hardcoded-literal collisions), came back empty on both after an extensive look, but independently found a genuine client-side race entirely outside either angle: `apps/web/src/WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s `mergeFreshMessages` (lines 99-106) is purely additive -- it only ever adds an id missing from `prev`, never removes one present in `prev` but absent from a fresher fetch. Three call sites rely on it to fold a freshly-fetched newest-page response into state: the connected-poll tick (every `CONNECTED_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, 10s), `handleSendTest`, and `handleRetry`. None of them account for a concurrent `handleDeleteMessage` or `handleClearHistory` removing something from `prev` while their own `listWhatsAppMessages` fetch is still in flight.

**Independent verification**: read every relevant call site directly. Confirmed the connected-poll tick's own `await listWhatsAppMessages(projectId)` (a real fetch) is the genuine yield point: if a user deletes a message (or clears the whole log) while that fetch is in flight, the delete/clear's own `await` resolves and calls `setMessages` first, emptying or shrinking `prev` -- then the poll's already-in-flight fetch resolves with its stale, pre-deletion page and calls `setMessages((prev) => mergeFreshMessages(prev, freshPage))`. Since every id in that stale page is now "missing" from the shrunk `prev`, `mergeFreshMessages` treats all of them as new and splices them back in. Confirmed this resurrection is permanent, not self-healing: the *next* poll tick fetches the genuinely up-to-date (now-empty) page, computes zero new ids, and returns `prev` unchanged -- so the wrongly-resurrected messages stay stuck until the panel is closed and reopened (the mount path does a hard `setMessages(messages)` replace, not a merge). Confirmed `handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory` never call `stopPolling()`/`stopConnectedPolling()` (grepped every call site of both) -- the existing `cancelled`/`cancelInFlightConnectedCheckRef` guard that already protects this same poll against a disconnect/reconnect race was never wired to protect against a delete/clear race at all. Confirmed this is a genuine race with two real, named `await`s racing each other (`listWhatsAppMessages` vs. `deleteWhatsAppMessage`/`clearWhatsAppMessages`, both real browser-side fetches) -- the "zero await between read and write ⇒ no race" rejection rule from round 423 is about this app's own single-process, synchronous-SQLite *server*, and doesn't apply to two independent client-side network calls racing in the browser. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` (the exported app) has no WhatsApp integration at all, so nothing to port there.

**The fix**: added `messagesVersionRef`, bumped by `handleDeleteMessage`/`handleClearHistory` the moment their own mutation succeeds server-side. Each of the three `mergeFreshMessages` call sites now captures the version right before its own `listWhatsAppMessages` fetch starts, and skips applying that fetch's result (`setMessages` is never even called) if the version changed while it was in flight -- the same ref-based in-flight-guard shape this file already uses for `cancelInFlightPollRef`/`cancelInFlightConnectedCheckRef`, just keyed to a different race.

**Tests**: added one new test building on the existing round-288 regex-extraction harness for `startConnectedPolling` (which already pulls the real function source out of the `.tsx` file and runs it via `new Function(...)` with stubbed dependencies) -- held the tick's own `listWhatsAppMessages` call open with a controlled promise (the established deterministic-race-test technique, not a timing-based sleep), waited for the fetch to actually be entered, then simulated `handleDeleteMessage`'s version bump before releasing it, and asserted `setMessages` was never called for that tick at all. Also updated the pre-existing round-288 test's own `new Function(...)` parameter list to supply the new `messagesVersionRef` dependency, since the extracted source now references it.

Writing this test's synchronization surfaced a test-construction mistake before it could be reported as a false failure: bumping the simulated version synchronously, immediately after invoking the tick function, raced ahead of the real code's own `const versionBeforeFetch = messagesVersionRef.current;` capture (which only runs after `getWhatsAppStatus`'s own `await` resolves, a full microtask turn later) -- landing the bump *before* the real "start of fetch" point instead of during it. Fixed by having the `listWhatsAppMessages` stub resolve a `fetchStarted` promise as its first synchronous action, and awaiting that in the test before bumping the version -- the same "wait for the held call to actually be entered" discipline round 424's own test already established, just applied to confirm the test's own timing was correct before trusting its result either way.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to HEAD (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred exactly: the new test failed with `1 !== 0` -- `setMessages` was called once despite the simulated version bump, the exact resurrection this fix prevents. Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **813 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix is web-only), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/db` (**127**), `@forge/shared` (**16**), `@forge/spec-engine` (**93**) stayed at their round-430 counts. Pushed as commit `6dc3b93`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It's a sibling in shape to round 422's "refresh()-vs-pending-delete resurrection" (both are "a stale async response resurrects a just-deleted item"), but mechanically distinct: round 422 was `EntityPanel.tsx`'s record table racing its own unconditional `refresh()` against a *deferred*-delete undo window; this round is `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s message log racing a *background poll's* additive merge against an *immediate* delete, with no undo window involved at all. Everything else still open from rounds 378-430 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 432: round 431's own fix left a fourth, unguarded call site -- "Load older messages" could still resurrect a just-cleared WhatsApp log

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed specifically at round 431's own fresh shape ("are there other client-side polling/refresh call sites that merge or replace state in a way that could race a concurrent user mutation"), re-examined `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` itself rather than looking elsewhere, and found that round 431's `messagesVersionRef` fix was incomplete: it names exactly three call sites in its own doc comment (the connected-poll tick, `handleSendTest`, `handleRetry`) and guards exactly those three, but `handleLoadMore` -- a fourth, pre-existing `listWhatsAppMessages`-then-`setMessages` call site -- was never touched at all.

**Independent verification**: read `handleLoadMore` directly and confirmed it has no `messagesVersionRef` check whatsoever: `const { messages: older, hasMore } = await listWhatsAppMessages(projectId, messages.length); setMessages((prev) => [...prev, ...older]); setHasMoreMessages(hasMore);` -- a plain, unconditional append, not even `mergeFreshMessages`. Confirmed "Load older messages" (gated only by `disabled={loadingMore}`) and "Clear history" (gated only by `disabled={clearing}`) are both always-rendered, independently-clickable buttons with no mutual exclusion. Confirmed the exploitable interleaving mechanically: click "Load older messages" (issues `GET .../messages?offset=2`, a real fetch) while that request is still in flight, click "Clear history" (issues `DELETE .../messages`, a real fetch) and let it resolve first -- `handleClearHistory` bumps `messagesVersionRef` and sets `messages` to `[]`. The still-in-flight "older page" fetch then resolves with its pre-clear data, and `handleLoadMore`'s unconditional append glues that stale page onto the now-empty `prev`, resurrecting the entire cleared history (and, per `handleClearHistory`'s own `setHasMoreMessages(false)`, this isn't limited to a single row the way a lone `handleDeleteMessage` race would be -- clearing wipes everything, so every id in the stale page looks newly resurrected). Confirmed this is the same client-side-race shape round 431 established (two independent browser fetches racing each other, not a server-side synchronous-DB race) and is a genuinely distinct gap from round 431's fix, not a re-opening of it: round 431's own enumeration of "three call sites" is the thing that was incomplete, not the mechanism it already closed for those three.

**The fix**: added the identical `messagesVersionRef` guard to `handleLoadMore` -- capture the version before the fetch starts, and skip both `setMessages` and `setHasMoreMessages` (the latter would also be stale data from before the clear) if the version changed while the fetch was in flight. Updated `messagesVersionRef`'s own doc comment to name all four guarded call sites instead of three, and to describe both failure shapes (`mergeFreshMessages`'s id-based splice, and `handleLoadMore`'s plain concat).

**Tests**: added one new full-render test (jsdom + React Testing Library, mirroring this file's existing "Load older messages" tests) that deterministically forces the race: holds the "older page" fetch open with a controlled promise, clicks "Load older messages", waits for the fetch to actually start (the button's own "Loading…" label, a real DOM signal), clicks "Clear history" and waits for the list to empty, then releases the held fetch. Writing this test surfaced a test-construction subtlety: `handleClearHistory`'s own `setHasMoreMessages(false)` unmounts the "Load older messages" button entirely once the log is cleared, so waiting for that button to leave its "Loading…" state (the first approach tried) is vacuously true the instant the button disappears -- it proved nothing about whether the stale fetch's continuation had actually run yet, and the test passed even against deliberately-reverted, unfixed code. Fixed by draining the microtask queue with `setImmediate` a few times after releasing the held fetch instead (the same technique `EntityPanel.test.ts` already uses for an identical need), which actually waits for `handleLoadMore`'s own continuation to run before asserting.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to round 431's own committed state (keeping the new test). The *first* version of the new test passed even against this unfixed code (the vacuous-wait bug described above) -- caught before being reported as a false confirmation, by noticing the suspiciously short test duration and re-deriving why the two states should have differed. After fixing the test's own wait mechanism, re-running against the same reverted file produced the correct, predicted failure (`1 !== 0`, the resurrected message). Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **814 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix is web-only), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. `@forge/db` (**127**), `@forge/shared` (**16**), `@forge/spec-engine` (**93**) stayed at their round-431 counts. Pushed as commit `fcb1e89`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed, and the enumeration gap it closes is worth naming as its own lesson: when a fix's own doc comment or implementation explicitly lists "the N call sites this protects," that list is itself a claim to verify, not just read -- grep for every other call site of the same underlying function (here, `listWhatsAppMessages`) before trusting that a guard's stated scope is its actual scope. Also reinforces round 425's "verify the regression-proof actually fails before the fix" lesson one level deeper: even a test explicitly built with the "hold the fetch open" technique can still fail to exercise the real race if some other piece of application state (here, `hasMoreMessages`) changes in a way that invalidates the wait condition being used to detect completion -- a passing regression-proof on a *known-unfixed* revert is itself a signal to re-examine the test, not just the fix. Everything else still open from rounds 378-431 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 433: BuildProgress showed a terminal "Build failed" banner (with live Retry/Back buttons) while the Debug Agent was still actively recovering from that exact failure

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at `BuildProgress.tsx`'s own existing round-? comment ("must reflect each agent's CURRENT status, not any failure ever seen") and at whether that fix was itself complete for every window it needed to cover, found that it protects a build *after* Debug's fresh success + Database's fresh success events have both arrived, but not during the real, multi-second gap between them.

**Independent verification**: read `pipeline.ts`'s migration-failure branch directly and confirmed the exact event order: it yields `{ agent: "Database", status: "failed" }` immediately, then `{ agent: "Debug", status: "running" }`, and only *after that* `await`s `requestSpecFix` -- a real Anthropic API call (`debug.ts`'s `fetchAnthropic`) that can genuinely take several real seconds -- before yielding Debug's success and a fresh Database success. During that whole window, `BuildProgress.tsx`'s `latestByAgent.get("Database")` is still `"failed"` (nothing newer has arrived yet for that agent), so `failedStep` was truthy and the component rendered the full terminal "Build failed" banner, with live, clickable Retry/Back buttons, at the exact same time the step list one row below it showed "Debug 🔧 running" -- a self-contradictory UI. Confirmed `Seed Data`/`QA` are the only other agents that ever yield `status: "failed"`, and neither has a recovery step after it (pipeline.ts `return`s immediately for QA; Seed Data's failure doesn't `return` at all, so it's never left mid-recovery the way Database/Debug's pair is) -- this transient-banner gap is specific to the Database/Debug pairing. Also confirmed (via grep across `api.ts`/`BuildProgress.tsx`) there is no `AbortController` or version-ref guard anywhere tying `handleRetry`'s fresh `run()` call to the still-open original stream, so clicking Retry during this window would fire a second `/build` or `/refine` POST that the server's own `activePipelines` guard correctly 409s -- compounding the misleading banner with a fabricated "already running" error while the real build keeps progressing underneath it.

**The fix**: `failedStep`'s computation now also requires that no agent is currently `"running"` anywhere in `latestByAgent`. `pipeline.ts` never starts a new step after yielding a genuinely terminal failure (it `return`s immediately in every case that doesn't recover), so any agent still showing `"running"` is proof-positive the pipeline hasn't given up -- a failed status only counts as the build's real, terminal failure once nothing is running anymore. This also closes the compounding Retry-race described above without a separate guard: the banner (and its Retry button) no longer renders during the only window that race could start from.

**Tests**: added one new test delivering the pipeline-shaped event sequence in two phases with a real held promise in between (holding back Debug's success + Database's fresh success + everything after, exactly like `pipeline.ts`'s own in-flight `await`) -- asserted the banner is absent and Debug's row still shows `"running"` during that held window, then released the rest and confirmed a normal recovered-success finish still renders every agent as succeeded.

Writing this test surfaced a hang, not a silent false-pass, when run against the deliberately-reverted (unfixed) code during the regression-proof step: the first version of the test's assertion compared a raw jsdom `Element` directly against `null` via `assert.equal(document.querySelector(...), null, ...)` -- the exact footgun this same test file's own standing comment already warns about elsewhere ("on failure, node:assert formats it with util.inspect(), and a jsdom element's huge, circular property graph makes that effectively hang"). Diagnosed by instrumenting the test with sequential debug markers to localize exactly which line stopped producing output, confirming the hang was neither a true infinite render loop in the component (a standalone repro script using the same unfixed component completed instantly) nor a dangling-promise issue (wrapping the release in `try/finally` didn't fix it), but specifically node:assert's formatter choking on the failing (non-null) `Element` it was asked to print. Fixed by reducing both DOM assertions to a boolean comparison first, matching the pattern this file already uses in its sibling "does not show the failed-build banner" test.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `BuildProgress.tsx` to the session scratchpad, reverted the component's `failedStep` computation to its pre-fix form (keeping the new, boolean-safe test). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: `AssertionError: false !== true` on "the 'Build failed' banner must not show while Debug is still actively running a recovery attempt" -- no hang, confirming the earlier hang really was the test's own construction, not the real component. Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran the full file and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **815 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix is web-only), plus both full suites passing standalone. Pushed as commit `44bc545`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It's a sibling in shape to round 432's "a prior fix's own stated scope needs independent verification," but applied to a *temporal* window instead of a call-site enumeration: `latestByAgent`'s "latest status" rule, from the fix that introduced it, is correct for every state the build can be in *after* a transition completes, but was never checked against the real, `await`-spanning window *during* a transition that the server's own pipeline genuinely has (Database failed → Debug running → real network wait → Debug/Database succeed). Also reinforces, from a new angle, the standing "a regression-proof that passes (or in this case hangs) against known-unfixed code is itself diagnostic information about the test, not the fix" lesson from rounds 425/432: here the signal was a hang rather than a vacuous pass, and the fix was the same documented DOM-assertion footgun this file had already named once before but I didn't check for in my own new test. Everything else still open from rounds 378-432 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 434: collapsed table groups leaked between two "Group by" fields that happened to share group keys

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at two fresh angles (incomplete call-site enumeration, and incomplete time-window coverage in a "latest status" computation), ruled out a long list of plausible candidates (client-side WhatsApp/BuildProgress races, already fully closed; HistoryPanel/GlobalSearchPanel staleness guards, already complete; backup.ts zip-entry collisions, already transitively prevented by `ProductSpecSchema`'s own collision checks; WhatsAppWebManager connect/disconnect races, already self-healing; sortKeys/fieldFilters/viewMode stale-field cleanup, all present and correct; roles/assumptions index races, already guarded) before finding a genuinely new gap in a not-yet-examined corner: `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` and its one caller in `EntityPanel.tsx`.

**Independent verification**: read `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` directly and confirmed its `keyFor(projectId, entityName)` scopes the persisted collapsed-group set by project+entity only -- no `groupFieldName` anywhere in the key. Read `entityFormatting.ts`'s `groupRecordsByField` and confirmed its group keys are field-independent: every boolean field's two groups are keyed by the literal strings `"true"`/`"false"` regardless of which field produced them, and an enum field's groups are keyed by its own raw enum-value strings (so two differently-named enum fields sharing a value, e.g. both using `"open"`, would collide the same way). Read `EntityPanel.tsx` and confirmed the effect that loads `collapsedGroups` from storage depends only on `[projectId, entity.name]` -- `groupFieldName` is absent from that dependency array -- and that the "Group by" `<select>`'s `onChange` handler only calls `setGroupFieldName`, never touching or reloading `collapsedGroups` at all. Confirmed the concrete failure mechanically: an entity with two boolean fields (e.g. `completed` and `urgent` -- very plausible for an AI-generated or refined spec), group by `completed`, collapse its "No" group (persists key `"false"` under `projectId:entityName`), switch "Group by" to `urgent` -- the stale `collapsedGroups` Set (still `{"false"}`) is never cleared or reloaded, so `urgent`'s own "No" group renders pre-collapsed even though the person never interacted with that grouping at all, silently hiding records with no visual explanation. Confirmed this is a wholly new gap, not a re-opening of any closed bug: it's not the already-fixed board-vs-table-view leak (that fix gave board columns and table groups separate stores, each still keyed only by project+entity -- it never added "which field is grouped by" to either key), and it's not the closed stale-field-cleanup pattern for `sortKeys`/`fieldFilters`/`viewMode` (those are about a field being *removed* from the spec; this is about two still-existing fields whose group keys collide because the preference key is missing a dimension entirely). Not a race condition -- purely synchronous client-side state/key-design bug, no `await` involved anywhere in it.

**The fix**: added `groupFieldName` as a third key segment in `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` (`${projectId}:${entityName}:${groupFieldName}`), threading it through `getCollapsedGroups`/`setCollapsedGroups`'s own signatures. Updated `EntityPanel.tsx`'s load effect to also depend on `groupFieldName` (so switching "Group by" re-reads the correct, now-field-scoped set) and its `toggleGroupCollapsed` to pass `groupFieldName` through to the persisted write. `purgeCollapsedGroupsForProject`'s existing prefix-based purge needed no change -- it still matches on `${projectId}:` regardless of the extra segment appended after entity name.

**Tests**: added one new full-render test (jsdom + React Testing Library) with a custom entity carrying two boolean fields (`completed`, `urgent`), grouping by `completed`, collapsing its "No" group, switching "Group by" to `urgent`, and asserting `urgent`'s own "No" group renders fully expanded (`aria-expanded="true"`, both of its one-record groups visible) rather than inheriting `completed`'s collapsed state. Also updated the signature of every other call site the new parameter touched (`EntityPanel.test.ts`'s existing collapse-persistence assertion, and all six `setCollapsedGroups`/`getCollapsedGroups` calls across `projectPreferenceCleanup.test.ts`'s three-project purge scenario) -- caught via `tsc`'s own arity errors, confirming the fix's scope by compiler rather than by trusting a manual grep alone.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` and `EntityPanel.tsx` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to their pre-fix state (keeping the new test; the now out-of-sync test files still type-checked fine against the reverted 2-arg signature's runtime behavior since `tsx` transpiles without enforcing call arity). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: `AssertionError: 'false' !== 'true'` on "switching 'Group by' to a different field must not carry over the first field's collapsed-group state." Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites. One `@forge/api` test failed on the first run with no relation to this web-only change; a second run passed all 400 cleanly, confirming a flake per this routine's own flake-handling rule.

Full suite green: **816 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix is web-only), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `5b38ac6`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It's a sibling in shape to round 433's "a derived-state computation needs to cover every case/window its own inputs can reach," but applied to a *key-design* gap instead of a temporal one: `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts`'s key was missing a whole dimension (which field produced the keys being stored) rather than missing a window during a transition. Everything else still open from rounds 378-433 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 435: Kanban board column collapse state leaked between fields once a schema edit changed which field drives the board

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at a fresh angle round 434 itself suggested ("does some OTHER persisted preference/cache key also need a dimension it's currently missing"), checked every sibling preference file (`columnWidths.ts`, `sortKeysPreference.ts`, `fieldFiltersPreference.ts`, `viewModePreference.ts`, `groupByPreference.ts`) and found one still open: `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts`, the Kanban board's own sibling to round 434's `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts`, left with the identical missing-dimension defect.

**Independent verification**: read `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` directly and confirmed `keyFor(projectId, entityName)` is scoped by project+entity only -- no board-field dimension, even though its own doc comment already explained the *cross-store* version of this exact risk ("board columns and table groups can be keyed by different fields, so sharing storage would conflate the two") as the reason it's a separate store from the table's own `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` -- without ever noticing the identical risk could occur *within* this one store alone. Read `entityFormatting.ts`'s `findBoardField` and confirmed it recomputes which field drives the board from the entity's *current* `fields` array on every render -- preferring a field literally named `"status"`/`"stage"`, else falling back to the first qualifying enum field -- and read `EntityPanel.tsx` and confirmed `boardField` is a `useMemo` keyed on `entity.fields` (line 864), while the `collapsedBoardColumns` load effect depended only on `[projectId, entity.name]`, and `toggleBoardColumnCollapsed` wrote through the same two-part key. Confirmed the concrete failure mechanically: an entity with one enum field `priority` (no name-hint match, so `findBoardField` falls back to it), collapse its `"low"` column, then a refine adds a `"status"` field (name-hint match) -- `findBoardField` now resolves to `status` instead, same `entity.name`, but the stale collapsed set (still `{"low"}`) is never reloaded or cleared, so `status`'s own `"low"` column renders pre-collapsed the instant it exists, purely because it happens to share a value string with the field that used to hold the board role. Confirmed no test file exists for this module at all (`collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.test.ts` doesn't exist), consistent with it having been missed by round 434's own fix and verification, which named only `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` and `EntityPanel.tsx`'s table-grouping call sites. Not a race -- purely synchronous client-side state/key-design, no `await` involved.

**The fix**: added `boardFieldName` as a third key segment in `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` (`${projectId}:${entityName}:${boardFieldName}`), mirroring round 434's fix exactly, threading it through `getCollapsedBoardColumns`/`setCollapsedBoardColumns`'s own signatures and expanding the doc comment to spell out why `boardField` needs this even though it's never a direct user choice the way `groupFieldName` is. In `EntityPanel.tsx`, introduced a `boardFieldName = boardField?.name ?? ""` local (a primitive, to avoid the load effect re-firing on every `useMemo` object-identity change rather than only on a genuine field-name change) and added it to the load effect's dependency array and to `toggleBoardColumnCollapsed`'s write-through call.

**Tests**: added one new full-render test (jsdom + React Testing Library) using `view.rerender(...)` to simulate a schema edit in place -- starts with an entity holding only a `priority` enum field, switches to board view, collapses `priority`'s `"low"` column, then rerenders with the *same* `entity.name` but a fields array that adds a `"status"` field (also having a `"low"` enum value) -- and asserts `status`'s own `"low"` column renders fully expanded (1 card, `aria-expanded="true"`) rather than inheriting `priority`'s collapsed state. Also updated the 6 other call sites `tsc`'s own arity errors caught (`projectPreferenceCleanup.test.ts`'s three-project purge scenario), the same discipline round 434 established.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` and `EntityPanel.tsx` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to their pre-fix state (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: `AssertionError: 0 !== 1` on "'status' field's own 'Low' column must not inherit 'priority' field's collapsed state." Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **817 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **400 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix is web-only), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `8d21724`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It's the direct sibling round 434 should have also caught (same defect shape, same codebase, a file sitting right next to the one that got fixed) -- confirming the value of round 434's own "missing key dimension" lesson generalizes across every persisted preference file, not just the one it happened to be found in first. Everything else still open from rounds 378-434 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 436: the exported standalone app's own generated EntityView had the same collapsed-group leak rounds 434/435 fixed in the live preview, in a third, untouched file

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at the "does a derived/cached value correctly track every input that can change it" vein rounds 432-435 kept mining, but pointed at fresh ground this time (codegen.ts's generated app mirroring every live-preview feature, rather than another live-preview preference file) found exactly that: `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` -- the generator that hand-duplicates EntityPanel.tsx's logic into the separately-maintained exported/standalone app's `EntityView` component -- still had the identical "group keys are field-independent" defect rounds 434 and 435 had already fixed in `apps/web/src/collapsedGroupsPreference.ts` and `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts`.

**Independent verification**: read `codegen.ts` directly and confirmed `getPersistedCollapsedGroups`/`setPersistedCollapsedGroups` (then at lines 1155-1167) and `getPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns`/`setPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns` (lines 1194-1206) -- both embedded inside codegen.ts's own giant template-literal string that becomes the generated `EntityView.jsx` -- were keyed by `entityName` alone, with no field dimension. Confirmed the generated template's own `groupRecordsByField` (line ~1885) has the exact same field-independent group keys as the live preview's (`"true"`/`"false"` for every boolean field, raw enum values for enum fields), and that neither the component's state initializers (`useState(() => new Set(getPersistedCollapsedGroups(entity.name)))`, no `groupFieldName`) nor its entity-switch reset effect (`}, [entity.name]);`, no `groupFieldName`/board-field dependency) ever re-scoped or reloaded on a "Group by" change. Confirmed via `git log` that neither round 434's commit (`5b38ac6`) nor round 435's (`8d21724`) touched `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` at all -- both fixes stayed entirely inside `apps/web/src/*`, leaving this independently-duplicated copy of the same logic in the exported app untouched. Not a race -- purely synchronous client-side state, no `await` involved.

**The fix**: mirrored rounds 434/435's fix exactly inside the generated template: `getPersistedCollapsedGroups`/`setPersistedCollapsedGroups` and `getPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns`/`setPersistedCollapsedBoardColumns` now take and key by the driving field name too (`entityName + ":" + fieldName`, plain string concatenation rather than a template literal, deliberately, since this code lives inside codegen.ts's own outer template literal and a literal `${...}` there would be interpolated by codegen.ts itself at generation time rather than by the generated app at runtime). Moved the state initializer for `collapsedBoardColumns` to call `findBoardField(entity.fields)` directly (the component's own `boardField` memo isn't computed yet at that point in the function body), removed the two field-agnostic resync calls from the bundled entity-switch effect, and added two new dedicated effects -- `useEffect(() => { setCollapsedGroups(...) }, [entity.name, groupFieldName])` and the board-column equivalent keyed on `[entity.name, boardField]` -- mirroring `EntityPanel.tsx`'s own separate-effects structure for this exact concern. Updated the write-through calls in `toggleGroupCollapsed`/`toggleBoardColumnCollapsed` to pass the current field name too.

**Tests**: added one new full-integration test (`codegen.test.ts`, using the file's own existing pattern of writing `generateExportFiles`'s output to a real temp directory, importing the actual generated `EntityView.jsx`, and driving it through `@testing-library/react` against a real jsdom `localStorage`) with a custom two-boolean-field entity (`completed`, `urgent`) -- groups by `completed`, collapses its "No" column, switches "Group by" to `urgent`, and asserts `urgent`'s own "No" group renders fully expanded rather than inheriting `completed`'s collapsed state. Also updated a stale doc comment on the existing board-column persistence test that still described the two stores as "keyed only by entity name."

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `codegen.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to its pre-fix state (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: `AssertionError: 'false' !== 'true'` on "switching 'Group by' to a different field must not carry over the first field's collapsed-group state." Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran the full monorepo build and both full suites clean.

Full suite green: **401 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **817 tests** in `@forge/web` (untouched -- this round's fix is API-only, inside `codegen.ts`'s generated-app template), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `6306c5d`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It generalizes rounds 434/435's own "fix the sibling file too" lesson one level further: the sibling to check isn't only another *preference file in the same directory* -- it can be an entirely separate, independently-maintained *copy of the same logic* in a different package (here, codegen.ts's hand-duplicated mirror of EntityPanel.tsx's behavior for the exported standalone app). Any future fix to EntityPanel.tsx's grouping/board/filter/sort logic should now also prompt checking whether codegen.ts's generated-app template carries the identical bug. Everything else still open from rounds 378-435 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 437: Business Twin's downloadable report listed mostLinkedRecord before mostActiveObservation, the reverse of how the live panel shows them

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, deliberately redirected away from the "missing key dimension"/"duplicated copy" vein rounds 432-436 had mined five rounds in a row, toward fresh functional areas (CSV import/export, Business Twin insights, WhatsApp content edge cases, checkpoint restore, accessibility, the refine/diff pipeline, security/IDOR, non-collapse EntityPanel/App.tsx features). It returned a structurally distinct find with no cache/preference-key/race/security angle at all: a plain ordering inconsistency between two renderings of the same data in the Business Twin feature.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/twinReport.ts` directly and confirmed `formatTwinReport`'s `allObservations` array (lines 46-51) placed `twin.mostLinkedRecord` before `twin.mostActiveObservation`, with a doc comment (lines 41-45) claiming this preserved "the same relative order they held before being split out." Read `apps/web/src/BusinessTwinPanel.tsx` directly (lines 190-218) and confirmed the live panel's own `<ul>` renders `mostActiveObservation`'s `<li>` (lines 197-207) *before* `mostLinkedRecord`'s `<li>` (lines 208-218) -- the reverse of twinReport.ts's order. Confirmed via `git show` (traced by the survey agent, spot-checked by reading the current state of both files) that this is a standing disagreement dating back to the commit that split `mostActiveObservation` out of the plain `observations` array: the panel's JSX put the new field before the pre-existing `mostLinkedRecord` block, reversing the panel's on-screen order, while twinReport.ts kept `mostLinkedRecord` first, preserving the prior order -- so the doc comment's claim became false for the panel without anyone updating it or twinReport.ts to match. Confirmed via reading `twinReport.test.ts` that no existing test covered both fields populated simultaneously, so nothing caught the drift. Not a race, not a key-design gap -- a plain two-renderings-of-one-fact-disagree bug: whenever both insights are present, the downloadable report a person shares (WhatsApp, email) lists them in the opposite order from what they saw on screen while reading it.

**The fix**: swapped `allObservations`'s order in `twinReport.ts` to put `mostActiveObservation` before `mostLinkedRecord`, matching the panel, and corrected the doc comment to describe the order by reference to `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`'s actual rendering rather than a historical claim that was no longer true.

**Tests**: added one new test to `twinReport.test.ts` constructing a `BusinessTwin` with both `mostActiveObservation` and `mostLinkedRecord` populated with distinguishable text, asserting via `report.indexOf(...)` comparison that `mostActiveObservation`'s bullet appears before `mostLinkedRecord`'s.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `twinReport.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to its pre-fix state (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]` on "mostActiveObservation must appear before mostLinkedRecord, matching the panel's order" (expected `true`, actual `false`), with all 7 other tests in the file still passing. Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran `tsc --noEmit`, the full `@forge/web` suite, the full `@forge/api` suite (unaffected), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`.

Full suite green: **818 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **401 tests** in `@forge/api` (untouched -- this round's fix touches only `apps/web/src/twinReport.ts`/`.test.ts`), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `e4c90b2`.

### Round 438: a self-referencing relation field's picker silently missed a record created after the panel first loaded

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, pointed explicitly at fresh ground given round 437's own closing note that CSV, checkpoint, diffAndMigrate, IDOR, and Business Twin insight logic all came back unusually heavily fortified with doc-comments addressing exactly this kind of edge case. It found a genuinely distinct gap in `apps/web/src/EntityPanel.tsx`: a relation field whose `relationTo` equals its own entity's name (a self-reference, e.g. a Category's own "parent category", an Employee's own "manager") is schema-legal -- `FieldSchema`'s relation refine only requires `relationTo` to be declared, never that it differ from the field's own entity -- but `relatedRecords[entity.name]`, the snapshot every relation-field `<select>` and display label renders from, is loaded once by its own effect and never refreshed by `refresh()`.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx` directly (lines 820-899) and confirmed `relatedRecords` is populated by a `loadRelated` effect depending on `[projectId, relationTargets]` -- never on the entity's own record data -- so creating/editing/deleting records never re-fires it. Read `refresh()` (lines 934-949) and confirmed it only calls `listRecords` for the entity itself and `setRecords(...)`, never touching `relatedRecords`; grepped every `setRelatedRecords` call site in the file (only 2: initial state and the one `loadRelated` effect) and every `await refresh();` call site (8, across create/edit, duplicate, bulk-update, CSV-import, board-move, and inline-edit) to confirm none of them update it. Read `FieldInput`'s relation branch (lines 665-682) and confirmed the `<select>`'s options come strictly from the `relatedEntityRecords` prop (i.e. the stale `relatedRecords` snapshot), both at the main form (line 2156) and the inline table-cell editor (line 2062). Read `packages/shared/src/index.ts` (lines 97-113) and confirmed `FieldSchema`'s only relation constraint is "must declare `relationTo`" -- nothing forbids it equaling the entity's own name. Confirmed a relation to a *different* entity never surfaces this: creating a record there requires switching to that entity's own tab, which remounts `EntityPanel` (keyed by `entity.name` in `App.tsx`) and refetches everything fresh -- a self-relation has no such remount. Grepped `EntityPanel.test.ts` for any `relationTo` equal to its own entity's name and found none, confirming the gap was untested. Not a race, not a key-design gap in a persisted preference -- a plain missing cache-invalidation case the "different entity" pattern happened to always paper over.

**The fix**: `refresh()` now also updates `relatedRecords[entity.name]` (to the same freshly-fetched, pending-delete-filtered record list it already uses for `records`) whenever `relationTargets.includes(entity.name)` -- i.e. whenever the entity is its own relation target. Per the now-established "duplicated copy" lesson from rounds 435/436, also checked and fixed the identical gap in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own hand-duplicated mirror of this same `refresh()` logic for the exported standalone app's generated `EntityView` component.

**Tests**: added one new full-render test to each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` (the latter via the established `generateExportFiles`/`writeGeneratedWebComponent`/`withRealLocalStorage` full-integration pattern) -- a self-referencing "Category" entity, create a new category through the live add-record form, then open a *different* existing category's edit form and confirm the just-created category now appears as a selectable option in its own "Parent Category" `<select>`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted both to their pre-fix state (keeping both new tests). Both predicted failures occurred cleanly: the web test's `waitForCondition` for the new option timed out, and the API test asserted `false` with `got options: …, Electronics` (no "Office Supplies"). Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran `tsc --noEmit`, the full `@forge/web` suite, the full `@forge/api` suite, and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`.

Full suite green: **819 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **402 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `2bb68a3`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It's a fresh bug shape from rounds 432-437's recent veins -- not a missing key dimension in a persisted preference, not a rendering-order disagreement, but a plain missing cache-invalidation case that every *cross*-entity relation happened to paper over by virtue of its own tab-switch remount, leaving only the one case (self-reference) genuinely uncovered. Everything else still open from rounds 378-437 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 439: the exported app's GlobalSearch Copy/Download report ignored "Show all", unlike the live preview's identical feature

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, steered away from every recently-mined bug shape (missing key dimension, duplicated-copy gap, rendering-order mismatch, missing cache-invalidation hidden by a silent "always remounts" assumption) and toward fresh ground (CSV edge cases, checkpoint restore, accessibility, the refine/diff pipeline, IDOR, WhatsApp content handling, Business Twin insight logic beyond ordering). It found a bug that is itself the same class round 437 closed -- a plain-text report disagreeing with what the live panel shows on screen -- but in a completely different feature (Global Search, not Business Twin) and a completely different mechanism (a missing function parameter in a hand-ported duplicate, not a historically-drifted array order).

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/searchReport.ts` directly and confirmed `formatSearchResults` takes an `expandedSamples: Record<string, EntityRecord[]>` parameter and uses `expandedSamples[result.entityName] ?? result.sample` (line 41) -- the live preview's own report correctly mirrors whatever a "Show all" expansion has put on screen. Read `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `formatGlobalSearchReport` (then at lines 3991-4008, inside the exported app's own generated-app template, explicitly commented as mirroring `searchReport.ts`) and confirmed its signature was only `(results, entities, query)` -- no `expandedSamples` parameter at all -- and it built every group's text strictly from `result.sample`, which the surrounding `searchAllEntities` always caps at 5 (`matches.slice(0, 5)`). Read the exported `GlobalSearch` component's own `expandedSamples` state (line 4073), `handleShowAll` (lines 4151-4168, which genuinely re-fetches and re-filters with no cap, confirmed correct), and the render path (line 4295: `const displayed = expandedSamples[result.entityName] ?? result.sample`, confirmed the on-screen table correctly shows every expanded match) -- then confirmed `handleCopy`/`handleDownload` (then at lines 4179-4194) both called `formatGlobalSearchReport(results, entities, query)`, never passing `expandedSamples` in at all. Confirmed via `grep` that these were the only 2 call sites. Confirmed via reading `codegen.test.ts` that the existing "Show all" test (line 7258) never touches Copy/Download afterward, and the existing Copy/Download test (line 5778) uses a dataset with only 1 record, so "Show all" never even appears there -- the combination was genuinely untested. Not a race, not a key-design gap, not an ordering mismatch -- a parameter the hand-ported duplicate simply never gained when the live preview's own `searchReport.ts` added it.

**The fix**: gave `formatGlobalSearchReport` an `expandedSamples` parameter (mirroring `searchReport.ts`'s `formatSearchResults` exactly -- `const displayed = expandedSamples[result.entityName] ?? result.sample;`, and the "…and N more" line computed from `displayed.length` instead of `result.sample.length`), and updated both `handleCopy` and `handleDownload` to pass the component's own `expandedSamples` state through.

**Tests**: added one new full-render test to `codegen.test.ts` -- search for "widget" against 7 matching Customer records (reveals the default 5-row sample), click "Show all" to expand to all 7 on screen, click Copy, and confirm the clipboard text includes every one of the 7 "Widget item N" labels with no stale "…and N more" line.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `codegen.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted it to its pre-fix state (keeping the new test). The predicted failure occurred cleanly: the copied text stopped at "Widget item 5" followed by the now-stale "…and 2 more" line, failing the assertion for "Widget item 6". Restored the file from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran `tsc --noEmit`, the full `@forge/api` suite, the full `@forge/web` suite (unaffected, confirming cross-package isolation), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`.

Full suite green: **403 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **819 tests** in `@forge/web` (untouched -- this round's fix touches only `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`/`.test.ts`), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `b25b787`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. It generalizes round 437's "two renderings of the same facts can silently disagree" lesson one level further: the disagreement doesn't have to be a historically-drifted array order inside one codebase -- it can be a hand-ported duplicate implementation of an entire feature (Global Search's report, mirroring the live preview's `searchReport.ts`) that simply never received a parameter the original later gained. Any future change to `searchReport.ts`'s own signature or behavior should now also prompt checking whether `codegen.ts`'s `formatGlobalSearchReport` duplicate needs the identical update. Everything else still open from rounds 378-438 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 440: a relation field's picker deterministically fell back to a raw, unvalidated number input on every mount while related records were still loading

**The survey**: Explore general-survey, directed at a wide range of fresh areas (IDOR/ownership checks, checkpoint restore, diffAndMigrate, CSV import/export, Business Twin, WhatsApp content handling, dialog accessibility, preference-store key design, and ~15 hand-duplicated codegen.ts functions diffed against their live-preview originals) found everything already exhaustively hardened by prior rounds. It did surface one strong candidate -- not a brand-new find, but a long-standing, explicitly-logged candidate from round 375's own closing notes ("the relation-field picker's brief raw-number-input flash before related records finish loading"), deprioritized at the time as lower-severity and carried unresolved through every subsequent round's "small open candidates" list (still visible verbatim in the hourly trigger prompt as "relation-picker flash... [375, 377]") -- confirmed still present in the current code. Picking up a standing small candidate when no fresh large one exists is itself one of this routine's own three sanctioned paths.

**Independent verification**: read `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `relatedRecords` state (line 826, `useState({})`) and its `loadRelated` effect (lines 869-899) and confirmed it only ever gets populated by a real `useEffect` with a genuine `await listRecords(...)` network call -- by React's own contract, a `useEffect` never runs synchronously on the first render. Read `FieldInput`'s relation branch (then at line 665: `if (field.type === "relation" && relatedEntity && relatedEntityRecords)`) and confirmed it required `relatedEntityRecords` to already be truthy to render the real `<select>`; read the fallback branch (`field.type === "number" || field.type === "relation"`) and confirmed a relation field with no `relatedEntityRecords` yet falls straight through to a plain, fully-editable `<input type="number">` with only a generic placeholder -- no options, no validation against a real related record. Read the full JSX return and confirmed the add/edit `<form className="record-form">` is rendered completely unconditionally, with no gate on either `loading` or `relatedRecords` -- the `{loading ? ... }` ternary (line 2242, after the fix) only ever wrapped the *table* section below it. This makes the raw-number window not a rare race but the deterministic first-paint state on every single mount of an entity with a relation field, for as long as the real network fetch takes -- a fast user, keyboard navigation, or autofill could submit an arbitrary, unvalidated foreign-key id during that window. Confirmed the byte-for-byte identical pattern in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s own hand-duplicated `FieldInput` for the exported standalone app. Grepped `EntityPanel.test.ts` for every relation-field test and confirmed all of them `await waitForCondition(...)` before ever inspecting the DOM, so none asserted anything about the pre-load window -- the flash itself had never been tested.

**The fix**: `FieldInput`'s relation branch now checks `relatedEntity` alone first; if `relatedEntityRecords` hasn't resolved yet, it renders a disabled, clearly-labeled loading placeholder `<select>` (new translation keys `entity.relation.loading` for he/en) instead of falling through to the raw number-input branch, and only becomes the real, option-backed `<select>` once `relatedEntityRecords` genuinely arrives. Applied the identical fix to `codegen.ts`'s hand-duplicated copy (using a plain "Loading…" string, since the exported app has no i18n).

**Tests**: added one new full-render test to each of `EntityPanel.test.ts` and `codegen.test.ts` -- an Order entity with a `courierId` relation field, with the Courier entity's own fetch held open via a manually-controlled promise. Confirms the relation field renders as a disabled placeholder (never a raw number input) while the fetch is held, then becomes the real select with the correct option once released.

**A footgun hit and fixed along the way**: the test's first draft compared a raw DOM node directly against `null` in `assert.equal`, which is the exact, already-documented node:assert hang footgun from round 433 (`util.inspect()` chokes on jsdom's circular property graph when building a failure diff against unfixed code) -- confirmed by reproducing the hang, then fixed by converting to a boolean comparison (`document.querySelector(...) === null`), matching the established pattern. A second, related issue surfaced during the same revert-verification: the held promise for the Courier fetch was only released after a later assertion, so when an *earlier* assertion threw first, the held promise (and the component's pending effect) stayed dangling and prevented the test process from exiting even after the test had already failed and reported cleanly. Fixed by releasing the held promise unconditionally in a `finally` block, regardless of where the test body throws.

**Collateral fix in codegen.test.ts**: changing `codegen.ts`'s relation-branch condition from `relatedEntity && relatedEntityRecords` to `relatedEntity` (with the loading check moved inside) broke two pre-existing regex-based tests that searched the generated source for that exact substring, or for `required={field.required}` within a now-longer branch than their fixed-length match window assumed. Both were updated to match the new source shape while preserving their original intent (confirmed both still pass against the fixed code).

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts` to the session scratchpad, `git checkout --` reverted each in turn (keeping the new tests), and confirmed each predicted failure occurred cleanly (`false !== true`, no hang, exit code 1 not a timeout) once the dangling-promise fix above was in place. Restored both files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then reran `tsc --noEmit`, the full `@forge/web` suite, the full `@forge/api` suite (including re-verifying the two collaterally-updated tests), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`.

Full suite green: **820 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **404 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `f29cdff`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed, and the round-375 "relation-picker flash" entry on the standing small-candidates list is now resolved. It's a different bug shape from rounds 432-439's recent veins -- not a missing key dimension, duplicated-copy gap, rendering-order mismatch, or missing cache-invalidation, but a plain missing loading-state guard on an unconditionally-rendered form -- and it doubled as a fresh demonstration of two already-documented lessons (the node:assert DOM-node hang footgun, and the need to release a held test promise unconditionally) rather than a new one. Everything else still open from rounds 378-439 remains open and unchanged.

### Round 441: a long, unbreakable field value (a URL, a long SKU, a long word) overflowed off the edge of a printed record or printed list, clipped with no visual indication

**The survey**: no fresh large candidate turned up this round. Per the routine's own rules, picking up a still-open entry from the standing small-candidates list is itself a legitimate path when that happens, so the round-377 "print overflow-wrap" entry — logged 64 rounds ago and never acted on — was investigated.

**Independent verification**: read `apps/web/src/styles.css` directly around the `.print-field` and `.print-list-sheet` rules (used by the printed single-record sheet and printed entity list, both rendered inside `@media print` blocks with `position: absolute; inset: 0`, i.e. no scrolling is possible once printed). Neither rule had `min-width: 0` (for the flex-item case) or `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. A flex item's `min-width` defaults to `auto`, which resolves to its min-content size — for text, the width of its single longest unbreakable token. Without the fix, one long token (a URL, a long SKU, a word with no spaces) forces the element wider than the available printed width, and the excess is silently clipped off the page. Cross-checked against 4 other places in the same stylesheet that already carry this exact `min-width: 0` + `overflow-wrap: anywhere` pairing (`.checkpoint-list li strong`, `.collab-list li strong`, `.whatsapp-log-body`, `.my-project-open strong`) — confirming this is an established, correct fix pattern to replicate, not a novel design call.

**The fix**: added `min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to `.print-field dd` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to the `.print-list-sheet th, .print-list-sheet td` rule in `apps/web/src/styles.css`. Checked `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` for a duplicated copy to mirror the fix into — confirmed via grep that it contains no `print-field`/`print-list-sheet` selectors at all, since the exported standalone app has no print feature (consistent with the standing "נבדק ונדחה" rejected-candidates list's "print בקוד מיוצא" entry) — so there was nothing to fix there.

**Tests**: jsdom has no layout engine, so a CSS-only overflow bug is structurally invisible to DOM-based assertions (the existing print-sheet tests already document this limitation and only check `textContent`/data wiring). Added a new regex-extraction test in `EntityPanel.test.ts` that reads `styles.css`'s own source text and asserts the `.print-field dd` rule contains `min-width: 0` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, and the `.print-list-sheet th, .print-list-sheet td` rule contains `overflow-wrap: anywhere` — mirroring the source-regex-test discipline already used extensively for `codegen.ts`'s generated-app template, applied here for the first time to this stylesheet.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the changed files, reverted `styles.css` via `git checkout --`, confirmed the new test failed with the exact predicted assertion mismatch, restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

Full suite green: **821 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **404 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Pushed as commit `5f015a6`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed, and the round-377 "print overflow-wrap" entry on the standing small-candidates list is now resolved. It's a plain missing-CSS-property gap rather than a new structural bug shape, and it's a straight replication of an already-established fix pattern used 4 times elsewhere in the same file — the main new wrinkle was recognizing that jsdom can't exercise CSS layout at all, so the regression test had to read the stylesheet's own source text rather than render anything. Everything else still open from rounds 378-440 remains open and unchanged, except that round 441's own survey separately flagged the round-379 `sanitizeZipEntryName` collision-risk entry as likely no longer a real candidate (already provably prevented upstream by `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`'s `ProductSpecSchema` refine) — left on the list for a future round to confirm and remove, not acted on in this round's trigger-prompt update.

### Round 442: confirmed the `sanitizeZipEntryName` collision candidate is provably dead, then closed the "export staleness marker" candidate (round 381, open for 61 rounds)

**Part one -- independently confirming a flagged candidate, not just trusting it**: round 441's survey had flagged (via a subagent, not direct code reading) that the round-379 `sanitizeZipEntryName` collision-risk candidate was likely already prevented upstream, and left it for a future round to confirm independently. Did that confirmation this round by reading the actual code rather than re-trusting the earlier claim. `sanitizeZipEntryName` (`apps/api/src/backup.ts`) only replaces `` [\\/:*?"<>|\u0000-\u001f] `` with `_` -- a narrow set, all of which are themselves non-alphanumeric ASCII characters. `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`, guarding `ProductSpecSchema`'s refine) replaces *every* non-alphanumeric character with `_` and lowercases -- a strictly broader transformation whose replaced-character set is a superset of `sanitizeZipEntryName`'s. Proved algebraically that this subset relationship means any two entity names that collide under `sanitizeZipEntryName` must also collide under `findSanitizedIdentifierCollisions` (every narrow-set replacement is also a broad-set replacement, and the broad transformation only identifies more strings together, never fewer). Then confirmed the enforcement path: the backup route (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts`) calls `requireProjectAccess` -> `getProject` -> `rowToProject`, which runs the *full*, throwing `ProductSpecSchema.parse()` (not the tolerant `tryRowToProject` variant used by listing endpoints) before `generateBackupZipEntries` ever sees the project. So a project spec that still has a live `sanitizeZipEntryName` collision can never pass that `parse()` call and therefore can never reach the backup code at all. Removed this entry from the trigger's standing small-candidates list (both occurrences) -- this is a genuine "confirmed dead, not a design-judgment skip" closure, the first of its kind on this list.

**Part two -- a real fix, since part one shipped no code change**: with that confirmation done, picked up the next-oldest item on the same standing list: "export staleness marker" (round 381, 61 rounds open). **Independent verification**: read round 381's own original roadmap entry -- a downloaded export ZIP carries no signal at all of when it was generated, so a user who re-opens an old export folder months after continuing to refine the live project has no way to tell the downloaded copy is now stale relative to the live one. Confirmed via direct reading of `generateExportFiles`/`renderReadme` in `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`: `renderReadme` builds the README from `project.name`/`project.description`/the entity list only -- no date, no version, nothing generation-time-dependent anywhere in any of the 20 exported files.

**The fix**: `generateExportFiles` now takes an optional `exportedAt: Date = new Date()` parameter (defaulted so the one real call site in `routes/projects.ts` needs no change), threaded through to `renderReadme(project, exportedAt)`. The README's opening paragraph now reads "Exported from Forge AI on **YYYY-MM-DD**... This is a snapshot taken at export time: if you keep refining the live project in Forge AI afterward, re-export it to get those later changes -- this folder does not update itself."

**Tests**: added a test in `apps/api/src/codegen.test.ts` that calls `generateExportFiles(project, exportedAt)` with two different explicit dates a day apart, asserting the README embeds each exact date and that the two renders differ -- proving the marker tracks real export time rather than being a hardcoded string, while staying fully deterministic (no reliance on the real system clock).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `codegen.ts`/`codegen.test.ts`, reverted `codegen.ts` via `git checkout --`, confirmed the new test failed with the exact predicted regex mismatch against the un-dated README text, restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green (149/149 in `codegen.test.ts` alone, then the full suite).

Full suite green: **821 tests** in `@forge/web` (unchanged), **405 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build`.

**Topic status**: both fixes are closed. The round-379 `sanitizeZipEntryName` candidate is removed from the standing list as provably dead (not merely unlikely). The round-381 "export staleness marker" candidate is closed with a real, tested fix. Everything else still open from rounds 378-441 (`wakeRetry.ts` idempotency, AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, duplicate `enumValues`, non-ASCII field name, Seed Data recycled-entity gap, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration) remains open and unchanged.

### Round 443: a duplicate value in a field's own `enumValues` silently duplicated every matching record's card/row across two identical board columns or table groups (round 375/377's standing "duplicate enumValues" candidate)

**The survey**: no fresh large candidate turned up. `FieldSchema.enumValues` (`packages/shared/src/index.ts`) is `z.array(z.string()).optional()` with no uniqueness constraint, and nothing else in this app ever edits `enumValues` directly (no UI lets a user add/rename an enum option), so the one realistic way a real project ends up with a duplicate is an AI-generated spec. Deliberately did **not** tighten `ProductSpecSchema`/`FieldSchema` to reject this: that schema is append-only in practice (its own doc comment) -- any stricter `.refine()` would make an already-stored project/checkpoint with this defect fail to parse from now on, which is sanctioned only for closing a real data-corruption hole (the SQL-identifier-collision refines), not a cosmetic/grouping bug.

**Independent verification**: grepped every render site that maps over `field.enumValues`/`boardField.enumValues`/`f.enumValues` in `EntityPanel.tsx` -- the add/edit form's enum `<select>`, the Kanban board card's move `<select>`, and the toolbar's filter-by-field `<select>` -- all three keyed `<option>` by the raw value with no dedup, so a duplicate rendered the same choice twice. Went further and checked `entityFormatting.ts`'s `groupByField` (the Kanban board's own column builder) and `groupRecordsByField` (the table's "group by" feature): both iterated `field.enumValues` directly with **no dedup at all**, so a duplicate value became its own column/group that filtered the *exact same records* as its twin -- every matching card/row rendered twice, once in each identical column/group. This is strictly worse than the `<select>` duplication: a real, visible data-rendering bug, not just a cosmetic dropdown repeat. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has byte-identical duplicated copies of all five sites (three `<select>`s plus both grouping functions) in the exported app's own `EntityView.jsx` template.

**The fix**: added one shared `uniqueEnumValues(values)` helper (order-preserving, `Array.from(new Set(values ?? []))`) exported from `entityFormatting.ts`, used by `groupByField`, `groupRecordsByField`, and all three `EntityPanel.tsx` `<select>` sites (replacing a first-draft EntityPanel-local copy of the same helper once the grouping-function gap was found, so there's exactly one canonical definition in the live preview). `codegen.ts` carries its own matching `uniqueEnumValues` in the generated `EntityView.jsx` template, used by its own five duplicated sites.

**Tests**: `entityFormatting.test.ts` gained a direct unit test for `uniqueEnumValues` plus regression tests for `groupByField` and `groupRecordsByField` confirming a duplicate declared value collapses to one column/group whose records aren't duplicated. `EntityPanel.test.ts` gained a full-component test covering all three `<select>` sites at once (filter dropdown, board move dropdown, add-form dropdown) with a genuinely duplicated `enumValues` array. `codegen.test.ts` gained a "real generated code via `new Function`" test (this file's own established standard) that extracts the generated `uniqueEnumValues` and calls it directly, then confirms all three `<select>` branches route through it via source matching. Fixed two pre-existing regex-extraction tests broken as collateral: one isolated-evaluated `groupByField` without `uniqueEnumValues` in scope (`ReferenceError`), and one of my own new assertions had a stray leading `{` that didn't match the toolbar `<select>`'s actual (non-JSX-container) call site.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all three changed implementation files (`entityFormatting.ts`, `EntityPanel.tsx`, `codegen.ts`), reverted them via `git checkout --`, confirmed every new/fixed test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (including a clean module-load `ReferenceError` for the files importing the now-missing `uniqueEnumValues`), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green: 102/102 in `EntityPanel.test.ts` alone, 150/150 in `codegen.test.ts` alone, then the full suites.

Full suite green: **825 tests** in `@forge/web` (+4), **406 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), plus a clean full monorepo `npm run build` and a clean `tsc -b` on `@forge/web`.

### Round 444: `diffAndMigrate` falsely reported a relation-target change when a field's `relationTo` oscillated back to the entity its FK had pointed at the whole time

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, after several rounds spent working through the standing small-candidates list, surfaced genuinely new territory: `packages/db/src/migrate.ts`, not previously examined by any prior round's survey. Its `prevField` branch (the path taken when a field exists continuously across two consecutive specs) compares `prevField.relationTo` -- the *immediately preceding* spec only -- against the new spec's `field.relationTo`, never against the column's actual physical foreign key. A field whose declared `relationTo` goes `Customer -> Vendor -> Customer` across three refines reports `relation_target_changed` correctly on the first hop, but *also* reports it on the third hop (reverting), even though the FK physically never left `Customer` for the whole sequence -- a false positive, not a real migration event.

**Independent verification**: read `diffAndMigrate`, `physicalColumnShape`, and the full `prevField` branch directly rather than trusting the subagent's framing, then wrote a standalone, throwaway repro script (`openDatabase` + `applyMigrations` + `diffAndMigrate` across three hand-built specs, deleted immediately after use, never committed) to independently reproduce the exact false report against the real code before changing anything. Confirmed: build reports `new_table`; `text -> number` reports `type_changed` correctly; `number -> text` (reverting to the original) reports `type_changed` *again*, even though `PRAGMA table_info` shows the physical column was `TEXT` the entire time and never actually changed. The same oscillation shape applies to `relation_target_changed`.

**A fix nearly made, caught before writing code**: the obvious generalization -- always compare against physical reality instead of the previous spec, for every field property -- would have been wrong. `sqlTypeFor` maps `text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` all onto the same `TEXT` SQL bucket, and `fieldTypeLabelForSqlType`'s reverse mapping can only ever report back `"text"` for that bucket, never `"enum"`/`"longtext"`/`"date"` -- a permanent, irreversible information loss once a value is only known physically. The existing, deliberately-tested `type_changed` test explicitly asserts `fromType: "enum"` for a single-hop enum -> text change, with its own comment confirming this is intentional policy ("reporting the change is not the same as applying it"), even though enum and text share a SQL bucket and nothing is ever at real storage risk. A physical-reality fix to `type_changed` would have either silently suppressed that legitimate report or produced an inaccurate `fromType: "text"` in its place. `relationTo`, by contrast, has no such ambiguity: every entity name maps to exactly one physical table name (`tableNameFor`), never collapsed the way SQL column types are. So the fix was scoped narrowly to `relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk` only, using the already-existing `physicalColumnShape` helper (the same one the sibling "reused column" branch already relies on) instead of the previous spec snapshot. `type_changed`'s identical oscillation bug is deliberately left unfixed this round, as a known, documented limitation rather than a silent gap -- added to the standing small-candidates list below.

**Tests**: added two tests to `migrate.test.ts`. One builds a three-spec Customer -> Vendor -> Customer sequence and asserts the reverting hop reports no changes at all (`[]`), while confirming the first hop still correctly reports `relation_target_changed` and the FK list still shows the original target throughout. The other builds a field whose `relationTo` names an entity that doesn't exist yet (so it starts with zero FK), then adds that entity without ever removing the field from the spec, and confirms `relation_missing_fk` is now correctly reported once the target starts existing -- a case the previous snapshot-only comparison would also have missed, since the field never left the spec and so never went through the "reused column" branch that already used physical reality.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `migrate.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the two new tests in `migrate.test.ts` in place), re-ran the suite and confirmed both new tests failed with the exact predicted mismatch -- a spurious `relation_target_changed Vendor -> Customer` reported where `[]` was expected, and the expected `relation_missing_fk` entry simply absent -- restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

Full suite green: **129 tests** in `@forge/db` (+2), **406 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged), **825 tests** in `@forge/web` (unchanged), a clean `tsc -b` on `@forge/web`, and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `cf28614`.

**Topic status**: the `relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk` oscillation false-positive is closed. A new standing small-candidate is opened: `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` branch has the identical oscillation false-positive, but is **not** safely fixable the same way, because `text`/`longtext`/`enum`/`date` collapse onto one indistinguishable SQL storage bucket -- any physical-reality-based fix there risks either breaking the existing, deliberately-tested enum -> text reporting behavior or requires persisting a field's full type lineage beyond one hop, which does not currently exist. This is a design/judgment-call item for a dedicated round, in the same spirit as `wakeRetry.ts`'s idempotency problem or `render.yaml`'s disk stanza, not a quick mechanical fix. `codegen.ts` was checked and confirmed to have no duplicated migration-diffing logic at all (the exported standalone app has no refine/Time-Machine history mechanism), so there was nothing to mirror this fix into. Everything else still open from rounds 378-443 (`wakeRetry.ts` idempotency, AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, non-ASCII field name, Seed Data recycled-entity gap, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration) remains open and unchanged.

Also confirmed the fix is safe and simple: `visibleRecords`/`records` -- the exact two values `formatEntityRecordCount` needs -- already exist under those same names in codegen.ts's generated component (`const visibleRecords = useMemo(...)` a few lines above the toolbar), computed identically (search + per-field filters + sort) to the live preview's own.
