### Round 446: Employee's bare `"worker"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary, everyday word `"coworker"`, spuriously fabricating an Employee entity and role for purely personal app descriptions

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch found a real instance of a bug class this file has already fixed five times before, in a spot none of those five passes caught. `domainEntities.ts`'s own header comment explicitly calls out "a bare keyword that's a plain substring of an unrelated, legitimate business word" as "pitfall 1", and the file already carries `\b`-bounded fixes for `order`/`stock`/`driver`/`patient`/`deals` (rounds 371-372) for exactly this shape. Employee's bare `"worker"` keyword -- present in both `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`'s Employee rule and `ROLE_RULES.Employee` -- was never given the same treatment, even though `"coworker"` contains it as a literal substring and is an extremely common word with nothing to do with HR/staff management.

**Independent verification**: read the exact keyword arrays at both sites directly, confirmed the precedent pattern by grepping the five existing `\b`-bounded fixes, then ran the real heuristic engine (`matchEntities`/`matchRoles` from `heuristic.ts`) against `"An app to split shared expenses with my coworker, like rent and groceries."` -- a pure personal expense-splitting description with no staff/HR concept anywhere in it. Confirmed the exact false positive: `matchEntities` returned `['Employee', 'Expense']` and `matchRoles` returned `['Employee', 'Admin']`, fabricating both a spurious Employee entity (its own table, with name/role/email/active fields) and a spurious Employee role, purely from the "worker" substring inside "coworker". This is the heuristic (zero-config, offline-fallback) spec provider -- the path used whenever no AI provider is configured -- so a real, reachable code path, not dead code.

**The fix**: changed the bare `"worker"` string to `/\bworkers?\b/` in both `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`'s Employee rule and `ROLE_RULES.Employee`, matching the exact pattern already used for the other five collisions. This surfaced a second, smaller gap: `ROLE_RULES`'s `keywords` field was typed `string[]` only (unlike `DomainEntityRule.keywords`, which already supports `string | RegExp`), and `matchRoles` in `heuristic.ts` called a raw `lower.includes(kw)` instead of the existing `matchesKeyword` helper that already handles both string and `RegExp` keywords. Widened `RoleRule.keywords` to `(string | RegExp)[]` and routed `matchRoles` through `matchesKeyword`, so the role side of the fix was possible at all -- without this, the entity-side fix alone would have left the spurious Employee *role* in place even after the spurious Employee *entity* was fixed.

**Tests**: added a test to `heuristic.test.ts`, following this file's own established pattern for the five earlier collision fixes (`provider.generate(...)` against a real description, asserting both the false-positive absence and that the real term still matches): confirms `"coworker"` alone triggers neither the Employee entity nor the Employee role, while a genuine staff-management description ("track every worker's shifts and hours") still matches both.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts` and `heuristic.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place), confirmed the test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the Employee entity assertion failed first, exactly as the un-fixed "coworker" repro had shown), restored from backup, confirmed both files byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

Full suite green: **94 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (+1), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **129 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), **407 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged), **825 tests** in `@forge/web` (unchanged), a clean `tsc -b` on `@forge/web`, and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `ced4d0c`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. No duplicated copy exists in `codegen.ts` to check -- `ROLE_RULES`/the heuristic spec engine is server-side spec-generation logic, not something the exported standalone app ever needs. No new standing candidate opened; this closes clean. ### Round 447: Course's bare `"courses"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary word `"discourses"`, spuriously fabricating a Course entity for plain discussion/forum app descriptions

**The survey**: a fresh Explore agent dispatch, explicitly pointed at `domainEntities.ts`'s recurring bare-substring collision class (now fixed six times -- `order`/`stock`/`driver`/`patient`/`deals`/`worker`), found a seventh, genuinely new instance at a location none of the prior six passes touched: Course's `keywords` array still carried a bare `"courses"` string, and `"discourses"` contains it as a literal substring.

### Round 448: MenuItem's bare `"dish"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary word `"dishonest"`, spuriously fabricating a MenuItem entity for consumer-protection/trust app descriptions

**The survey**: this round's Explore agent was explicitly instructed to make `domainEntities.ts`'s bare-substring collision class the top priority -- the class had just turned up two new, genuinely distinct instances in the two immediately preceding rounds (446's `worker`, 447's `courses`), despite having been considered "fixed" after each of five earlier passes. Rather than a single targeted check, the agent did a systematic sweep of the remaining unbounded keyword strings across `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES` and `ROLE_RULES`, verifying each candidate collision with real code before reporting. It found MenuItem's bare `"dish"` colliding with `"dishonest"`, and -- while sweeping -- also surfaced four further unverified-but-plausible candidates it had independently confirmed with the same method: Product's `"product"` vs `"production"`, Vehicle's `"mechanic"` vs `"mechanical"`, and Service's `"treatment"` vs `"mistreatment"` and `"service"` vs `"disservice"`. Only the strongest one (`dish`/`dishonest`) was picked for this round's fix, per the one-bug-per-round discipline; the other four are recorded below as a new standing small-candidates entry for a future round, already pre-verified so a future pass can skip straight to the fix.

**Independent verification**: read the MenuItem entity rule directly (`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`, `domainEntities.ts`) -- notably, this exact rule already carries a doc comment from an earlier round explaining why the Hebrew keyword `"מנה"` was deliberately left bare-unbounded-but-excluded (it's a literal prefix of `"מנהל"`/manager, one of the most common words in Hebrew business descriptions), showing the collision risk in this specific entity had already been scrutinized once for Hebrew but never re-checked for English. Ran the real `matchEntities` function against `"An app for a consumer watchdog group to track dishonest sellers and scam reports."` -- a pure consumer-protection description with zero restaurant/food content. Confirmed the exact false positive: `matchEntities` returned `['MenuItem']`, fabricating a spurious MenuItem entity (name/description/price/category/available fields, with a Starter/Main/Dessert/Drink enum) purely from the "dish" substring inside "dishonest". Confirmed MenuItem has no presence in `ROLE_RULES`, so this is a single-site fix.

**The fix**: changed the bare `"dish"` string to `/\bdish(es)?\b/`. Unlike round 447's `"courses"` (where adding a singular form would have introduced a worse collision), here the `(es)?` suffix is safe and actually necessary to preserve existing, correct behavior: the plural `"dishes"` was never a separate keyword, but it matched anyway as an accidental side effect of the old bare-substring `.includes()` check (since `"dish"` is itself a literal prefix of `"dishes"`). A plain `/\bdish\b/` without the suffix would have been a silent regression, breaking the "dishes" case the old buggy code happened to get right. Verified both forms explicitly in the new test.

**Tests**: added a test to `heuristic.test.ts`, following the established pattern for the seven earlier collision fixes: confirms `"dishonest"` alone does not trigger the MenuItem entity, while both `"dish"` and `"dishes"` in a genuine restaurant/cafe description still do (the two-form check specifically guards the regression risk described above).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place), confirmed the test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the MenuItem false-positive returned, exactly as the un-fixed "dishonest" repro had shown), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

### Round 449: Product's bare `"product"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary word `"production"`, spuriously fabricating a Product entity for creative/media app descriptions

**The candidate**: no new survey needed this round -- round 448's survey had already pre-verified four corroborating `domainEntities.ts` bare-substring collisions and left them as a ready-to-fix standing small-candidate list. Picked the first: Product's `"product"` keyword.

**Independent verification**: read the Product entity rule directly (`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`, `domainEntities.ts`) -- confirmed `"product"` was still a bare, unbounded string (alongside `"inventory"` and the already-`\b`-bounded `/\bstock(s)?\b/` from an earlier round's fix of the same rule), and confirmed Product has no presence in `ROLE_RULES`, making this a single-site fix like round 448's. Ran the real `matchEntities` function against `"An app for a video production studio to manage clients and bookings."` -- a pure creative/media description with zero retail or inventory content. ### Out-of-band (after round 450): a 280+ round mystery finally resolved -- "שרדג תלת מימד" meant a decorative 3D graphic

Since round 114, every single round's closing message to שלומי re-asked an unanswered question: "מה עם ה'שרדג תלת מימד'?" ("what about the 'שרדג three-dimensional'?") -- a fragment from an old message whose meaning was never clear, carried forward unresolved for over 330 rounds. In this window she finally replied, first with the equally terse "תלת מימד התקן" ("three-dimensional device/install"), then -- after a clarifying question -- with "תצוגה תלת-מימדית ב-Forge AI" (a 3D display in Forge AI), and after a second clarifying question specifically on what should actually render in 3D: "גרפיקה/קישוט תלת-מימדי לעמוד (דקורטיבי)" -- a decorative 3D graphic for the page.

**Built**: a small rotating cube on the home screen, directly above the title, built entirely from CSS 3D transforms (`perspective`, `transform-style: preserve-3d`, six absolutely-positioned `.hero3d-face` divs each `rotateX`/`rotateY`/`translateZ`'d into place, and a `@keyframes hero3d-spin` animation) -- no WebGL or three.js dependency, consistent with this app's existing all-CSS visual-design conventions. Uses the theme's own `--accent`/`--accent-deep`/`--accent-soft` CSS variables for its face gradients, so it adapts to light/dark mode automatically with zero extra code (already confirmed working in both rounds' own screenshots, see below). The wrapping element is `aria-hidden="true"`, matching round 91's accessibility-pass precedent that a purely decorative element should never reach the accessibility tree. The animation is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` -- the cube stays visible at a fixed angle rather than vanishing outright, since only the *motion*, not the shape itself, is what reduced-motion users need to avoid. A `@media (max-width: 480px)` block shrinks the cube on small screens, matching this file's existing mobile-breakpoint convention.

**Verified visually, not just via source-text assertions**: since jsdom has no real 3D rendering engine to exercise, and Playwright isn't installed in this repo as a project dependency (round 314's standing note), used the globally pre-installed Playwright + Chromium (`/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright`, `/opt/pw-browsers`) to build a standalone HTML harness with the *exact* CSS extracted verbatim from `styles.css` and the real JSX markup structure, then actually screenshotted it in headless Chromium: confirmed a genuine rotating 3D cube with correct per-face shading in light mode, confirmed correct rendering with the dark-mode CSS variable overrides substituted in, and confirmed two screenshots taken 1.5 seconds apart under a `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` browser context are pixel-identical -- proving the animation is genuinely disabled, not just slowed down.

**Tests**: two new tests. One reads `App.tsx`'s own source (the same `readFileSync`-based regex-extraction discipline every other test in `App.test.ts` already uses, since this file never does a full React render) to confirm the `.hero3d` wrapper sits immediately before the home screen's `<h1>`, carries `aria-hidden="true"`, and has exactly 6 `.hero3d-face` children. The other reads `styles.css` directly (round 441's established CSS-only-bug discipline) to confirm `.hero3d-cube` declares `transform-style: preserve-3d` and references the `hero3d-spin` animation, that the `@keyframes hero3d-spin` rule exists, and that the `prefers-reduced-motion` override actually sets `animation: none` on `.hero3d-cube` rather than merely existing as an empty block.

Full suite green: **829 tests** in `@forge/web` (+2), with `@forge/spec-engine` (102), `@forge/shared` (16), `@forge/db` (129), and `@forge/api` (411) all unchanged, a clean `tsc -b` on `@forge/web`, and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `79c30bf`.

### Round 454: Vehicle's bare `"garage"` keyword was a genuinely ambiguous whole word, spuriously fabricating a Vehicle entity for "garage sale" descriptions -- a new collision shape, not a substring-in-a-word

**The candidate**: the last standing small-candidate from rounds 448-450: Vehicle's `"garage"` keyword, noticed in passing during round 450 but deliberately left unverified at the time (one-bug-per-round discipline).

**Independent verification**: read the Vehicle entity rule directly (`DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`, `domainEntities.ts`) -- confirmed `"garage"` was still a bare, unbounded string alongside `"vehicle"`, `"vehicles"`, `"fleet management"`, the already-fixed `/\bmechanic(s)?\b/`, and `"car dealership"`. Ran the real `matchEntities` function against `"An app for a neighborhood community to coordinate an annual garage sale, listing items each household wants to sell."` -- a pure community/household-sale description with zero vehicle content. Confirmed the exact false positive: `matchEntities` returned `['Property', 'Vehicle']`, fabricating a spurious Vehicle entity purely from the word "garage" inside the everyday phrase "garage sale" (the `Property` match, from "household"/"neighborhood", was separately expected and not investigated further).

**Why this needed a different fix than the previous ten collisions**: every prior fix in this class (order/stock/driver/patient/deals/worker/courses/dish/product/mechanic/treatment/service) was a bare keyword that was a literal *substring inside a longer, unrelated word* ("mechanic" inside "mechanical"), so a `\b`-bounded `RegExp` was sufficient -- the longer word simply stopped matching as a whole word. "garage" is different: it is a complete, correctly-spelled whole word in *both* "repair garage" (the real signal) and "garage sale" (the false one), so `/\bgarage\b/` alone still matches both -- `\b` boundaries can't distinguish the two phrases. The fix instead needed a negative lookahead, `/\bgarage\b(?!\s+sales?\b)/`, which excludes only the specific "garage sale"/"garage sales" phrase while leaving every other use of the word (including "garage door", "repair garage", "auto garage") matching exactly as before. Verified the regex in isolation against all four cases (garage sale, garage sales, repair garage, garage door) before touching the entity rule.

**Tests**: added a test to `heuristic.test.ts` following the established pattern, but covering both the singular and plural phrase: confirms neither `"garage sale"` nor `"garage sales"` alone triggers the Vehicle entity, while a genuine auto-repair description worded to avoid this rule's other keywords (`"vehicle"`, `"mechanic"`, `"fleet management"`, `"car dealership"`) still does -- isolating that the real match genuinely still comes from "garage" itself. Re-read the edit's result in full before running any test, per rounds 452-453's lesson about silent corruption from a string-replacement edit -- no corruption found this round. Confirmed via an isolated test run that the two pre-existing tests mentioning "garage" (the general domain-recognition test and the WorkOrder-disambiguation test) remained green and unaffected.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place), confirmed the test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the Vehicle false-positive returned, exactly as the un-fixed "garage sale" repro had shown), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

### Round 457: verified and fixed the last of round 455's two unverified candidates -- Property's bare `"listing"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary word `"enlisting"`, spuriously fabricating a Property entity for nonprofit/volunteer-outreach descriptions

Ran the real `matchEntities` function against `"An app for a nonprofit coordinator enlisting local volunteers and businesses to sponsor an annual charity run."` -- a pure nonprofit/volunteer-outreach description with zero real-estate content. Confirmed the exact false positive: `matchEntities` returned `['Property', 'Donation', 'Volunteer']`, fabricating a spurious Property entity purely from the "listing" substring inside "enlisting" (the `Donation`/`Volunteer` matches, from "sponsor"/"volunteers", were separate, expected matches not investigated further).

**The fix**: changed the bare `"listing"` string to `/\blisting(s)?\b/`, the fifteenth fix of this exact pitfall-1 shape in this file. The `(s)?` suffix preserves the existing plural match.

**Tests**: added a test to `heuristic.test.ts` following the established pattern: confirms `"enlisting"` alone does not trigger the Property entity, while both `"listing"` and `"listings"` in genuine real-estate descriptions (worded to avoid this rule's other keywords -- `"property"`, `"real estate"`, `"apartment for rent"`) still do. Re-read the edit's result in full before running any test, per round 456's lesson that this discipline has caught real corruption before -- no corruption found this round, confirming it isn't always needed but is cheap insurance each time.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `domainEntities.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place), confirmed the test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the Property false-positive returned, exactly as the un-fixed "enlisting" repro had shown), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

### Round 458: broadened the collision-class survey past `domainEntities.ts` and found `badgeTone` misclassifying common negated business statuses ("Unpaid", "Unapproved", "Undelivered", ...) as positive -- the opposite of their meaning

**The candidate**: with both of round 455's `domainEntities.ts` candidates closed and that file surveyed twice already, ran a fresh Explore survey this round targeting the same bug shape (a bare `.includes()` keyword that's a literal substring of an unrelated, or in this case semantically *opposite*, word) in every OTHER file across the monorepo that does keyword-based text classification -- explicitly excluding `domainEntities.ts`/`heuristic.ts`. It surveyed every `.includes()`/`.indexOf()` call doing free-text classification across `apps/web/src`, `apps/api/src`, `packages/db`, `packages/spec-engine`, correctly ruling out exact-equality enum checks, ID-array lookups, and intentional free-text search boxes (`matchesSearch`, `filterCheckpoints`, etc.) as out of scope. It surfaced `badgeTone` in `entityFormatting.ts` (duplicated in `codegen.ts`'s exported-app template): `POSITIVE_WORDS` contains `"paid"`, `"approved"`, `"confirmed"`, `"delivered"`, `"qualified"`, `"shipped"`, each a literal substring of an everyday negated business-status term (`"unpaid"`, `"unapproved"`/`"disapproved"`, `"unconfirmed"`, `"undelivered"`, `"unqualified"`/`"disqualified"`, `"unshipped"`) that isn't listed in `NEGATIVE_WORDS`.

**Independent verification**: read `badgeTone` and its two word lists directly in `entityFormatting.ts` -- confirmed the file already has exactly this bug shape fixed once before, for `"inactive"` vs `"active"` (with a code comment explaining the negative-first check order and why `"inactive"` had to be added to `NEGATIVE_WORDS`), but none of the other `POSITIVE_WORDS` entries' negated forms were ever added. Ran the real `badgeTone` function directly against all nine `POSITIVE_WORDS` entries with `"un-"`/`"dis-"` prefixes -- every single one came back `"positive"`, confirming the false classification is systemic, not a one-off. Checked whether any built-in domain entity's own enum currently uses these exact negated values (none do today), but confirmed `badgeTone`'s own doc comment states its purpose is specifically to also classify freeform AI-generated enum values -- exactly where these ordinary English status terms would appear.

**The fix**: added the realistic negated counterparts to `NEGATIVE_WORDS` in both `entityFormatting.ts` and its duplicated copy in `codegen.ts`'s exported-app template string: `"unpaid"`, `"undelivered"`, `"unconfirmed"`, `"unapproved"`, `"disapproved"`, `"unqualified"`, `"disqualified"`, `"unshipped"` -- scoped to terms with clear real-world business-status currency (skipped lower-plausibility forms like `"unwon"`/`"uncompleted"`/`"unsuccess"`, which aren't standard English status words). This mirrors the exact pattern the file already established for `"inactive"`, rather than introducing new generic prefix-detection logic.

**Tests**: added a test to `entityFormatting.test.ts` immediately after the existing `"Inactive"` regression test, following its exact structure: asserts each negated form is `"negative"` and its positive root is still `"positive"`, covering all eight new entries in one test. Confirmed `codegen.ts`'s copy is inside a template-literal string (the generated app's own source), so the multi-line array edit there is just plain JS text with no backtick/`${}` escaping concerns.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `entityFormatting.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `entityFormatting.test.ts` in place), confirmed the test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (`badgeTone("Unpaid")` returned `"positive"` instead of `"negative"`), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran green.

Full suite green: **830 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **108 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **129 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), **411 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged, confirming `codegen.ts`'s module still loads and parses cleanly after the template-string edit), a clean `tsc -b` on `@forge/web`, and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `66e5bf0`.

### Round 459: extended round 458's broadened survey further and found `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS`'s bare `"ssn"` hint was a literal substring of the ordinary field names `"businessName"`/`"className"`, spuriously docking the build's Security score

**The candidate**: no known `domainEntities.ts` candidate remained, so ran a fresh Explore survey continuing round 458's direction -- specifically targeting any other `WORDS`/`KEYWORDS`/`HINTS`/`PATTERNS`-style array doing substring-based text classification anywhere in the monorepo, outside everything already fixed (`domainEntities.ts`/`heuristic.ts`, `entityFormatting.ts`'s `badgeTone`). The survey found two candidates: `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` in `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s `runSecurityScan` (bare `"ssn"` colliding with `"businessName"`/`"className"`), and `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` in `heuristic.ts` (bare `"stripe"` colliding with `"pinstripe"`/`"striped"`, affecting only generated open-question wording). Picked the higher-confidence, higher-impact one: `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` directly affects a warning count and a displayed numeric Security score, and sits right next to an *existing* regression test for the exact same array fixing the identical bug shape for the sibling `"secret"` hint (`"secretary"` false positive, fixed in an earlier round) -- the fix was applied only to `"secret"`, leaving `"ssn"` as a plain, unguarded substring check.

**Independent verification**: read `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS` and `runSecurityScan` directly in `pipeline.ts` -- confirmed `"ssn"` was still a bare string, checked via `lowerName.includes(hint)` against the field's lowercased name. Wrote a standalone Node script reproducing the exact check with the real array and confirmed: `"businessName"` and `"className"` both return `true` (false positive -- lowercased they contain `"ssn"` as `"busine`**`ssn`**`ame"` / `"cla`**`ssn`**`ame"`), while `"lastName"`/`"firstName"`/`"companyName"` correctly return `false`. Both false-positive field names are entirely ordinary and plausible (e.g. on a Vendor/Customer entity, or a literal "class name" field on a Course entity) -- neither has anything to do with a Social Security Number. Checked the other four bare-string hints (`"token"`, `"apikey"`, `"api_key"`, `"creditcard"`) individually for a real colliding English word and found none -- only `"ssn"` collides.

**The fix**: mirrored the exact shape already used for the sibling `"secret"` hint in this same array (a regex against the field's *original*, un-lowercased name, since field names are camelCase/snake_case identifiers where capitalization marks word starts, not prose where lowercasing is safe): `/(?:(?<![a-zA-Z])ssn|SSN)(?![a-z])/`. Verified the regex directly with node against nine inputs before applying it: correctly matches `"ssn"`, `"SSN"`, `"userSSN"`, `"ssn_number"`, and `"ssnNumber"`, while correctly rejecting `"businessName"`, `"className"`, `"lastName"`, and the less-common title-case variant `"customerSsn"` (an acceptable corner case, matching this established pattern's own known limitation for unusual capitalization styles).

**Tests**: added a test to `pipeline.test.ts` immediately after the existing `"secretary"` regression test, mirroring its exact structure (same entity-building boilerplate, same assertion shape): confirms `"businessName"`/`"className"` are never flagged, while `"ssn"`/`"userSSN"`/`"ssn_number"` are all still flagged, and the warning count is exactly 3 (not 5). Re-read the edit's result in full before running any test, per the standing discipline from rounds 452-458 -- no corruption found this round. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicated copy of `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS`/`runSecurityScan` (the security scan is a build-pipeline-only feature, not part of the exported standalone app), so this is a single-site fix.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `pipeline.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `pipeline.test.ts` in place), ran only the new test and confirmed it failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the first assertion -- `"businessName"` must not be flagged -- failed, `expected: true, actual: false`, exactly as the un-fixed repro had shown), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran the full `@forge/api` suite green.

Full suite green: **412 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **830 tests** in `@forge/web` (unchanged), **108 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **129 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `045434a`.

### Round 460: verified and fixed round 459's unverified candidate -- `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`'s bare `"stripe"` keyword was a literal substring of the ordinary word `"striped"`/`"pinstripe"`, spuriously recommending Stripe as a payment provider for clothing-store descriptions

**The candidate**: round 459's survey left one candidate standing without an independent repro -- `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`'s bare `"stripe"` in `heuristic.ts` colliding with `"pinstripe"`/`"striped"`. Picked it up this round since no larger "ready" candidate was open.

**Independent verification**: read `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS` and `buildOpenQuestions` directly -- confirmed `"stripe"` was still a bare, unbounded string matched via `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS.some((kw) => lower.includes(kw))`. Ran the real `HeuristicSpecProvider.generate()` end-to-end (not just the array in isolation) against three descriptions: a tailor description mentioning "pinstripe suits" (matched only the `Customer` entity, not in `BILLING_ENTITY_NAMES`), and a clothing-store description mentioning "striped shirts" (matched only `Product`, also not a billing entity) -- both wrongly got `"Which payment provider should this use?"` recommending Stripe. A control test proved the exact cause: the clothing-store description with `"striped"` swapped for `"plaid"` (otherwise byte-identical) correctly got `"Does this application need to accept payments?"` with `"No payments"` -- isolating the single word as the trigger. Checked the array's other five English entries (`"payment"`, `"invoice"`, `"billing"`, `"subscription"`, `"checkout"`) individually for a real colliding word and found none.

**The fix**: changed `"stripe"` to `/\bstripe\b/` in `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`. Since `buildOpenQuestions`'s own check used a hardcoded `lower.includes(kw)` (which throws on a `RegExp` argument -- `String.prototype.includes` requires a non-regex argument), reused this same file's existing `matchesKeyword(lower, kw)` helper (already used for `DOMAIN_ENTITY_RULES`/`ROLE_RULES`, supporting both `string` and `RegExp` entries) instead of inlining a second type check. Verified the regex directly with node first: matches `"stripe"` and `"the stripe api"`, correctly rejects `"stripes"`, `"striped"`, `"pinstripe"`, `"stripey"` -- "Stripe" the company is never referred to in the plural, so no `(s)?` suffix was added, unlike the `(s)?`-suffixed fixes in `domainEntities.ts`.

**Tests**: added a test to `heuristic.test.ts` immediately before the existing Hebrew-detection test, following the file's established end-to-end style (constructing a real `HeuristicSpecProvider` and asserting on its actual `generate()` output, not a mocked keyword list): confirms both `"striped"` and `"pinstripe"` descriptions get `"No payments"`, while a real `"...integrates with stripe to process customer payments"` description still gets `"Which payment provider should this use?"` recommending `"Stripe"`. Re-read the edit's result in full before running any test, per the standing discipline from rounds 452-459 -- no corruption found this round. Confirmed `codegen.ts` has no duplicated copy of `PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`/`buildOpenQuestions` (spec-generation-time logic only, not part of the exported standalone app).

**Regression-proof**: backed up `heuristic.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in `heuristic.test.ts` in place), ran only the new test and confirmed it failed with the exact predicted mismatch (`"Which payment provider should this use?"` instead of `"Does this application need to accept payments?"` for the striped-shirts description), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff`, then re-ran the full `@forge/spec-engine` suite green.

### Round 461: moved past the keyword-collision bug class (fully exhausted across rounds 458-460) and found "jump to record" only cleared its own filter/view-mode override in memory, letting a tab switch silently resurrect them and re-hide the record

**The candidate**: with the keyword-collision bug class fully closed (both round 458's and 459's surveys' candidates now fixed), ran a fresh general-purpose Explore survey this round, explicitly excluding `domainEntities.ts`/`heuristic.ts`/`entityFormatting.ts`'s `badgeTone`/`pipeline.ts`'s `SENSITIVE_FIELD_HINTS`, looking broadly for a DIFFERENT kind of bug (races, stale-closures, duplicated-copy drift, pagination/boundary bugs, missing guards, UI state bugs) across the rest of `apps/web/src` and `apps/api/src`. It surfaced `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `highlightRecordId` effect (the "jump to record" feature wired from `GlobalSearchPanel`/Business Twin/WhatsApp log): it clears `fieldFilters`/`viewMode` with bare `setFieldFilters({})`/`setViewMode("table")`, while every OTHER mutator of these same two pieces of state in this file (the Clear-filters button, the view-mode buttons) always writes through to `fieldFiltersPreference.ts`/`viewModePreference.ts`'s persisted storage too.

**Independent verification**: read the highlight effect and confirmed the asymmetry directly in the source -- grepped every `setFieldFilters(`/`setViewMode(` call site in the file and confirmed the highlight effect's two calls are the only ones that never call `setFieldFiltersPreference`/`setViewModePreference`. Confirmed the actual remount mechanism the bug depends on: `App.tsx` renders `<EntityPanel key={entity.name} .../>` filtered to just the active entity, so switching entity tabs fully unmounts and remounts `EntityPanel` (not a prop update on a long-lived instance) -- and the mount-time effects that load `fieldFilters`/`viewMode` from persisted storage run unconditionally on every mount, independent of `highlightRecordId`. This confirms the full repro chain without needing a live browser: jump to a record that's hidden by an active filter/view-mode → effect clears both in memory and reveals it → switch to another tab and back → the fresh `EntityPanel` mount reloads the still-stale persisted filter/view-mode → the record is silently hidden again, with no reload needed and no error.

**The fix**: routed the two clears through the same persisting setters the manual controls already use -- `setFieldFilters(() => { setFieldFiltersPreference(projectId, entity.name, {}); return {}; })` and `setViewMode(setViewModePreference(projectId, entity.name, "table"))` -- rather than inventing new logic, mirroring the exact pattern already established at the Clear-filters button and view-mode buttons a few hundred lines below in the same file.

**Duplicated-copy check**: confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts`'s `EntityView` component (the exported standalone app's own copy) has the byte-identical bug, not a drift between the two files -- it was never fixed in either. The exported app's entity-tab switcher swaps in a different component function per entity with no explicit `key`, which React also treats as a full unmount/remount, so the identical reproduction path applies there too. Fixed the same way, using `codegen.ts`'s own `setPersistedFieldFilters`/`setPersistedViewMode` helpers (keyed by `entity.name` alone, since the exported app is single-project) -- confirmed this is plain JS text inside the template-literal string with no backticks/`${}` introduced.

**Tests**: added a test to `EntityPanel.test.ts` immediately after the existing highlight test, following its established pattern (a real component tree, a real fetch mock, `rerender` to simulate an already-mounted jump) -- but extended to also directly assert on `getFieldFilters`/`getViewMode`'s actual persisted-storage return values (not just the DOM), and to `unmount()` + fresh-`render()` afterward (mirroring the established "survives an unmount+remount" idiom from the view-mode/collapsed-group persistence tests) to confirm the cleared values don't get resurrected on the next mount. Added a lighter content-assertion test to `codegen.test.ts` (matching this file's established style of asserting on generated source rather than full jsdom rendering for most features) confirming the generated `EntityView.jsx` now contains the same persisting-setter calls.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests in place), confirmed each new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (`EntityPanel.test.ts`: `getFieldFilters` returned `{status: "new"}` instead of `{}`; `codegen.test.ts`: the content-assertion regex didn't match the still-bare `setFieldFilters({})` call), restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` on both, then re-ran the full `@forge/web` and `@forge/api` suites green.

Full suite green: **831 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **413 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **109 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **129 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `7a3d6e7`.

### Round 462: found a sibling bug to round 461's fix, in the exact same effect -- "jump to record" never cleared table grouping either, so a record filed inside a collapsed group would silently fail to actually appear

**The candidate**: continued the mutator-asymmetry/UI-state survey round 461 started, this time applying the same technique systematically to every other `use*Preference.ts`-style module in `apps/web/src` (`groupByPreference.ts`, `sortKeysPreference.ts`, `collapsedGroupsPreference.ts`, `collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts`, `columnOrder.ts`, `columnWidths.ts`, `columnVisibility.ts`, the three `recentSearches` modules, theme/language) -- grepping every mutator of each piece of state and checking whether all of them wrote through to the persisting setter. All of those were symmetric and clean. The survey found something different: not a mutator skipping its own persister, but an *omission* -- the highlight effect round 461 just finished auditing still never touches `groupFieldName`/`collapsedGroups`, a third, independently-persisted piece of state that hides rows exactly as effectively as the two it already clears.

**Independent verification**: read the highlight effect as it stands after round 461's fix and confirmed it clears `search`, `fieldFilters`, and `viewMode`, but never `groupFieldName`. Grepped every `setGroupFieldName(` call site in `EntityPanel.tsx` and confirmed only two exist: the mount-load effect and the "Group by" `<select>`'s `onChange` (which persists via `setGroupByField`) -- the highlight effect touches neither. Read the table body's rendering and confirmed a collapsed group's records are skipped entirely (`{!collapsed && group.records.map(renderRecordRow)}`) -- not hidden with CSS, never placed in the DOM at all -- so the scroll-into-view follow-up effect's `querySelector` finds nothing and silently no-ops (no error, no fallback, no visible result). Confirmed the identical gap in `codegen.ts`'s `EntityView` -- its own doc comment claims to mirror "the round 461 fix," but the grouping omission was never noticed there either, so it's not a drift between the two copies, just an oversight present in both from the start.

**The fix**: added `setGroupFieldName(setGroupByField(projectId, entity.name, ""))` to the highlight effect in both files (using `codegen.ts`'s own `setPersistedGroupField(entity.name, "")` equivalent there), clearing grouping entirely the same way the filter/view-mode clears already do -- matching the established "what else could hide this row" reasoning from round 461 rather than inventing new logic (e.g. auto-expanding just the one collapsed group).

**Tests**: added a test to `EntityPanel.test.ts` immediately after round 461's test: groups the table by status, collapses the group containing the target record, confirms the record's row is genuinely absent from the DOM beforehand, then jumps to it and confirms grouping is cleared entirely (not just that one group re-expanded), the persisted `groupByPreference.ts` storage is cleared too, and the record's row is both present and highlighted afterward. Added a lighter content-assertion test to `codegen.test.ts` matching this file's established style for `EntityView`, confirming the generated source now calls the persisting setter. Re-read both edits in full before running anything -- no corruption found.

**Regression-proof**: backed up both `EntityPanel.tsx` and `codegen.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new tests in place), confirmed each new test failed with the exact predicted mismatch (`EntityPanel.test.ts`: `getGroupByField` returned `"status"` instead of `""`; `codegen.test.ts`: the content-assertion regex didn't match the still-missing `setGroupFieldName(setPersistedGroupField(...))` call), restored both from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff` on both, then re-ran the full `@forge/web` and `@forge/api` suites green. One `@forge/api` run showed a single unrelated failure while running concurrently in the background alongside the `@forge/web` suite; a clean sequential re-run of the full `@forge/api` suite came back 414/414 with no code changes in between, confirming it was a one-off resource-contention flake, not a regression from this fix.

Dispatched an Explore agent to audit every such effect it could find: `EntityPanel.tsx`'s `highlightRecordId` effect (the one already fixed through round 462), `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `selectedIndex` scroll effect, `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx`'s and `WhatsAppPanel.tsx`'s own "jump to record" affordances, and `HistoryPanel.tsx`/`App.tsx` for anything comparable. The agent's verdict: no gap anywhere. `EntityPanel.tsx`'s effect clears everything that can hide a row in the table render path; `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx`'s `selectedIndex` only ever selects from the already-fully-rendered `results` array (nothing to clear); `BusinessTwinPanel.tsx` and `WhatsAppPanel.tsx` have no independent reveal mechanism of their own -- both just delegate outward to `EntityPanel`'s mechanism via `onJumpToRecord`; `codegen.ts`'s duplicated `EntityView`/`GlobalSearch` mirror both correctly, no duplicated gap.

**Independent verification**: rather than trust the agent's report outright, read `EntityPanel.tsx:1347-1383` directly -- confirmed `visibleRecords` is gated only by `search`+`fieldFilters` (both cleared), and `groupField` resolves to `null` when `groupFieldName` is cleared to `""` (no field is ever named the empty string), which makes `recordGroups` `null` and routes the table through its flat, ungrouped render path -- so `collapsedGroups`' own persisted state becomes moot rather than needing a separate clear. Also read `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:295-301,417-425` directly and confirmed every entry in `results` is rendered unconditionally in its `.map`, with `selectedIndex` clamped to `results.length - 1` -- nothing in that array can be hidden, so there's nothing for the scroll effect to miss.

**A second, different angle**: rather than stop at one clean result, pivoted to a different bug shape in the same neighborhood -- the one rounds 434/435 fixed (`collapsedGroupsPreference.ts`/`collapsedBoardColumnsPreference.ts` were keyed too coarsely, by entity alone, when the UI state they persisted also depended on *which field* you'd grouped/boarded by). Dispatched a second Explore agent to audit all ~25 `localStorage`-backed preference modules in `apps/web/src` for the same "key missing a dimension, stale value gets misapplied" shape: `sortKeysPreference.ts`, `fieldFiltersPreference.ts`, `groupByPreference.ts`, `columnOrder.ts`/`columnWidths.ts`/`columnVisibility.ts`, `viewModePreference.ts`, `entityTabOrder.ts`, every `recentSearches` variant, theme/language, and more. Verdict: no new gap. Everywhere a stored value's inner key is a field's own `name` (not its `label`), two fields can never collide since only `label` is renameable server-side; everywhere the read path exists, it already validates the stored value against the entity's current field set and drops/falls back on a stale reference rather than blindly applying it.

**Independent verification**: spot-checked the load-bearing claim across both agents' reports -- that only a field's `label`, never its stable `name`, is renameable -- by grepping every `renameFieldLabel` call site (`FieldLabelEditor.tsx:71`, `apps/web/src/api.ts:281`) and reading the server-side route it hits (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:1154`): `fields: e.fields.map((f) => (f.name === field.name ? { ...f, label: parsed.data.label } : f))` -- confirms only `label` is ever mutated, `name` never changes, so no two fields can ever come to share the `name` these stores key their inner maps by.

No project-count limit exists anywhere in the app for an asymmetry to hide behind, either.

### Round 464: checkpoint restore silently discarded the exact migration-hazard diagnostics /build and /refine already give, letting a restored boolean field misrender arbitrary stored text as true/false with zero warning

**The candidate**: followed round 463's own suggested direction (b) -- a dedicated audit of checkpoint restore semantics, an area never previously audited restore-specifically (prior rounds 419/420 covered checkpoint rename/deletion, not restore itself). Dispatched an Explore agent to read the restore route end-to-end and interrogate its real-world semantics: what restore actually moves (spec pointer only, never record data), whether data created after a restored checkpoint survives (yes -- additive-only migrations never drop columns/tables), whether there's a confirmation dialog (yes), whether restoring "out of order" relative to other checkpoints behaves correctly (yes), whether restore itself checkpoints the pre-restore state (no, but moot since build/refine already did), and whether a race with an in-flight build/refine is guarded (yes, `activePipelines`). Six of seven questions came back clean. The seventh found a real gap: the restore route calls `diffAndMigrate` -- the exact same function `/build` and `/refine` call -- but throws its return value away completely, where `pipeline.ts` always turns that same return value into a loud "Note: ... kept the original database column type" warning shown live during every build and refine.

**Independent verification**: read the restore route directly (`apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:774-799` before the fix) and confirmed `diffAndMigrate(db, project.id, project.spec, checkpoint.spec);` on its own line, return value unused, versus `pipeline.ts`'s `const changes = diffAndMigrate(...)` which goes on to build a `type_changed`/`relation_target_changed`/`relation_missing_fk` warning message. Grepped `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `restoreCheckpoint` (returns only `{ project }`) and the one existing restore test in `app.test.ts` (asserts only on `project.spec.entities`) -- nothing anywhere captures this. Read `packages/db/src/repository.ts:80`'s `rowToRecord`: `field.type === "boolean" ? Boolean(value) : value` -- confirmed `Boolean("any non-empty string")` is always `true`, so a field that was boolean at checkpoint time, retyped to text under the same name by a later refine (physical column stays INTEGER the whole time -- SQLite can't cheaply retype it, which is exactly what `type_changed` exists to report), then restored back to boolean, would have every record with real stored text silently rendered as a checkmark, with the one diagnostic that would explain it computed and thrown away right at the one call site that needed it most.

**The fix**: extracted the inline "kept the original type/relation target" message-building logic `pipeline.ts` already had into a new exported `describeMigrationHazards(changes: MigrationChange[]): string` helper in `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` (re-exported from `packages/db/src/index.ts`), producing byte-identical text to what `pipeline.ts` built inline before (confirmed via a dedicated unit test pinning the exact string). `pipeline.ts` now calls this helper instead of its own three-way inline concatenation -- a pure refactor, not a behavior change. The restore route now does `const changes = diffAndMigrate(...)`, builds `const migrationWarning = describeMigrationHazards(changes).trim()`, and returns `{ project: updated, migrationWarning: migrationWarning.length > 0 ? migrationWarning : null }`. `apps/web/src/api.ts`'s `restoreCheckpoint` return type now includes `migrationWarning: string | null`, and `HistoryPanel.tsx` stores it in a new `restoreWarning` state (cleared at the start of every restore, set from the response) and displays it as a `role="status"` paragraph right under the existing error display -- matching this codebase's own established convention (`BuildProgress.tsx`'s own doc comment: "showing the real message verbatim") of showing this exact raw English diagnostic text as-is rather than reinventing a translated version of it. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicated Time Machine/checkpoint feature at all (platform-only, like `pipeline.ts`/`heuristic.ts` before it) -- no second copy to check.

**Tests**: added a unit test to `packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts` pinning `describeMigrationHazards`'s exact output for the empty case, each individual hazard type, and all three concatenated (proving the extraction changed nothing about `pipeline.ts`'s existing behavior). Added an HTTP-level integration test to `apps/api/src/app.test.ts` that engineers the exact "same field name, different physical type" scenario deterministically via direct `packages/db` calls (`insertProject`/`diffAndMigrate`/`insertCheckpoint`/`updateProjectSpec`) rather than relying on the heuristic spec generator to happen to produce it from free text, then hits the real restore HTTP route and asserts `migrationWarning` is present with the right field/table/type text, plus a control case (restoring a checkpoint whose spec already matches current state) asserting `migrationWarning` comes back `null`, not an empty string. Required widening `withServer`'s test helper to also hand the test its `db` handle for this direct setup -- backward compatible, since every existing single-param callback is still a valid narrower implementation of the now two-param callback type. Added a `HistoryPanel.test.ts` test confirming the warning text actually renders after a restore, is absent beforehand, and is replaced (not left stale) by a later restore that reports none.

**Regression-proof**: backed up all six changed implementation files (`migrate.ts`, `index.ts`, `pipeline.ts`, `projects.ts`, `api.ts`, `HistoryPanel.tsx`), reverted them via `git checkout --` (keeping the three test files' new tests in place), and confirmed three distinct, exactly-predicted failures: `migrate.test.ts` failed at module load (`SyntaxError: ... does not provide an export named 'describeMigrationHazards'`), `app.test.ts`'s new restore test failed its own `migrationWarning must be present` assertion, and `HistoryPanel.test.ts`'s new test timed out waiting for warning text that no longer renders. Restored all six files from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q` against each backup copy, then re-ran every affected suite clean.

Full suite green: **833 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **415 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **130 tests** in `@forge/db` (+1), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **109 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `d48ae25`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed. Checkpoint restore's own remaining six semantic questions (data survival, confirmation, out-of-order restore, self-checkpointing, pipeline race, diff-panel accuracy) were all independently confirmed correct and need no further work. Everything still open from rounds 378-462 (`wakeRetry.ts` idempotency, AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, non-ASCII field name, Seed Data recycled-entity gap, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration, `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` oscillation) remains open and unchanged. One related, narrower finding surfaced but deliberately NOT fixed this round (separate scope): `BuildProgress.tsx`'s Database-agent detail-list renderer (`build.detail.database.*`) maps `relation_missing_fk` entries through the same ternary branch as `type_changed` (its final `else`), which would render `undefined → undefined` via `c.fromType`/`c.toType` for a `relation_missing_fk` entry (which only ever sets `toRelationTo`, never `fromType`/`toType`) -- a candidate for a future round, not pursued here to keep this round's fix scoped to the restore-route gap actually investigated and verified.

### Round 465: `BuildProgress.tsx`'s Database-step detail list mislabeled `relation_missing_fk` entries as `type_changed`, rendering "undefined → undefined" instead of the real relation target

**The candidate**: round 464's own closing note flagged this directly -- while investigating checkpoint restore, the same audit noticed `BuildProgress.tsx`'s local `MigrationChangeDetail` type never learned about `relation_missing_fk`, the fifth `MigrationChange` variant (`packages/db/src/migrate.ts`), reported when a relation field reuses a column that was never linked to anything. This is the exact bug shape round 396 already fixed once for `relation_target_changed` (documented in this file) -- a sibling variant added later to the real type never got threaded through this one other place in the codebase that switches on `MigrationChange.type` by name.

**Independent verification**: read `MigrationChangeDetail`'s type union directly (`apps/web/src/BuildProgress.tsx:154` before the fix): `"new_table" | "new_column" | "type_changed" | "relation_target_changed"` -- `"relation_missing_fk"` is simply absent. Read the render ternary (lines 226-232): `new_table` → `new_column` → `relation_target_changed` → final `else`, which assumes `type_changed` and reads `c.fromType`/`c.toType`. Confirmed in `packages/db/src/migrate.ts` that a `relation_missing_fk` entry only ever sets `toRelationTo` (never `fromType`/`toType`/`fromRelationTo`), so the final `else` branch would render `${c.fromType} → ${c.toType}` as literally `undefined → undefined`. Reproduced this exact string by writing a test with a `relation_missing_fk` detail entry before the fix and confirming the predicted output.

**The fix**: added `"relation_missing_fk"` to `MigrationChangeDetail`'s type union, and a dedicated ternary branch (`c.type === "relation_missing_fk" ? ... : ...`) rendering `${c.table}.${c.column} (→ ${c.toRelationTo})` -- matching the "no `from`, only `to`" shape `pipeline.ts`'s own `describeMigrationHazards` message already uses for this same variant. Added matching Hebrew and English i18n keys (`build.detail.database.relationMissingFk`), wording consistent with the existing three sibling keys. Confirmed `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicated copy of this rendering logic at all (platform-only AI-build-watching UI, not part of the exported business app) -- no second copy to check.

**Tests**: added a regression test to `BuildProgress.test.ts` directly mirroring round 396's own `relation_target_changed` test -- renders a `relation_missing_fk` detail entry, expands the Database step's detail panel, and asserts the real relation target (`→ Driver`) appears, `undefined` never appears, and the wording is specific to this variant rather than reusing the unrelated "Field type changed" label.

**Regression-proof**: backed up `BuildProgress.tsx` and `language.ts`, reverted both via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), confirmed the new test failed with the exact predicted string -- `"Field type changed but the database column was left unchanged: entity_proj1_Order.driverId (undefined → undefined)"` -- restored both files, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then re-ran the isolated test, the i18n key-completeness scanner (`language.test.ts`), and the full suite, all green.

Full suite green: **834 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **415 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged), **130 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **109 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `962eb48`.

### Round 467: a new entity's required relation to an existing-but-emptied entity permanently failed to seed, with no error ever shown to the user

**The candidate**: round 466's own closing note suggested a genuinely fresh, unconstrained Explore survey after two clean rounds in a row had exhausted both the duplicated-union-type pattern and Business Twin's insight functions. Dispatched an Explore agent explicitly instructed to avoid every previously-exhausted bug shape and investigate a fresh area in depth. It surfaced a real, reproducible bug in seed-data generation: `pipeline.ts`'s Seed Data step only ever reseeded an entity that was BOTH brand-new per the current migration diff AND currently empty. An entity that already existed but had since been emptied out (e.g. the user deleted every record through the normal UI) was permanently ineligible for reseeding -- and `packages/db/src/seed.ts`'s required-relation guess for a required field is a static "row 1". When a later refine adds a new entity with a required relation to that now-empty existing entity, every single seed insert for the new entity throws a real SQLite `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, permanently leaving it with zero seeded rows and no error ever surfacing to the user (a separate, documented, out-of-scope gap in `BuildProgress.tsx` masks non-terminal Seed Data failures whenever the pipeline still reaches a final `Forge: success` event).

**Independent verification**: read `apps/api/src/pipeline.ts`'s eligibility filter directly and confirmed the agent's claim exactly -- `newEntityNames.has(...) && countRecords(db, project.id, e) === 0`. Read `packages/db/src/seed.ts`'s `seedValueFor`'s `"relation"` case (`return field.required ? 1 : null;`) and its own doc comment, which only discusses a target that already has rows from an earlier build, not a target that currently has zero rows. Read `orderForSeeding` and confirmed it only orders entities that are already in the same batch array passed to it -- confirming the fix needed to add the existing-but-emptied target into the same seeding batch, not seed it separately.

**The first fix attempt was incomplete, caught by the test it wrote before being trusted**: the first implementation walked the required-relation graph from every new entity to find and include any existing-but-currently-empty target in the same seeding batch (cycle-safe via a visited set), gated by the same `countRecords === 0` check. Writing the regression test and running it against this first version failed -- `Seeded 2 record(s), but 2 failed: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`, because `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` never reuses a deleted rowid even once a table is completely empty: reseeding a deleted-then-emptied Customer table lands on ids 3, 4, ... not 1, so the seeder's static "row 1" guess for the dependent Invoice entity's required relation was still a dangling foreign key. A manual repro script confirmed this exact failure mode directly before the real fix was written.

**The real fix**: in addition to the graph walk above (needed to decide *which* entities belong in the batch), each generated record's required-relation field value is now resolved against whichever real row the target entity actually has at insert time (`listRecords(db, project.id, target)[0].id`) rather than trusting the static guess -- correct both for a target seeded fresh in this batch (still id 1, same as before) and for one reseeded after being emptied (correctly picks up its real new id). A self-relation or genuine cycle where no real row exists yet at resolution time is left exactly as fragile as before (no regression there, no new fallback invented).

**Tests**: added a test to `apps/api/src/pipeline.test.ts` reproducing the exact scenario end-to-end: build a project with a Customer entity (auto-seeds 2 rows), delete every Customer record via the real `deleteRecord` path, refine to add a new Invoice entity with a required relation to Customer, and assert the Seed Data step now reports `status: "success"` (not a FOREIGN KEY failure) with both Invoice and Customer actually holding seeded rows afterward.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `pipeline.ts`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping the new test in place), confirmed the new test failed with the exact predicted `"seeding must not report any FK-constraint-violation failures"` assertion mismatch (actual: `"failed"`), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then re-ran the full `@forge/api` suite clean. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicated copy of the Seed Data step or any of this logic at all (platform-only AI-build feature, same precedent as `pipeline.ts`/`heuristic.ts` before it) -- no second copy to check.

Full suite green: **834 tests** in `@forge/web` (unchanged), **416 tests** in `@forge/api` (+1), **130 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **109 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `534a2c3`.

**Topic status**: this fix is closed for the backend root cause. A related, narrower finding surfaced during verification but deliberately NOT fixed this round (separate scope, matching the round-464→465 precedent of deferring a related-but-distinct issue): `BuildProgress.tsx`'s `onComplete` fires solely based on the last event being `Forge`/`success`, immediately navigating the user away before any earlier non-terminal agent-step failure's `failedStep` banner can ever be seen on screen -- meaning a Seed Data failure (or any other non-terminal step's failure) that doesn't stop the overall build is silently invisible to the user today, even now that the specific FK-constraint cause this round closed is fixed. Flagged as the standing candidate for round 468. Everything else still open from rounds 378-466 (`wakeRetry.ts` idempotency, AI-label language mismatch, checkpoint pruning, render.yaml disk stanza, `listRecords` pagination, non-ASCII field name, `diffAndMigrate`'s `type_changed` oscillation, `CollaboratorsPanel` email enumeration) remains open and unchanged.

### Round 468: a non-terminal agent-step failure (e.g. Seed Data) that doesn't stop the build was silently invisible to the user, with no banner or notice anywhere

**The candidate**: round 467's own closing note flagged this directly as the fresh standing small candidate -- `BuildProgress.tsx`'s `onComplete` fires solely based on the last event being `Forge`/`success`, immediately navigating the user away before any earlier non-terminal agent-step failure could ever be seen, even though the pipeline keeps going (and often still reaches `Forge: success`) past a failure in a step like Seed Data that doesn't itself block the build.

**Independent verification**: read `BuildProgress.tsx`'s mount effect directly (`useEffect(() => { if (!finished) return; ... if (last?.agent === "Forge" && last.status === "success") onComplete(...); }, [finished])`) and confirmed it only ever inspects the LAST event, never checking whether any earlier agent's own latest event is still `"failed"`. Read the component's own extensive existing doc comments and a dedicated prior-round test (`"BuildProgress does not show a 'Download build summary' button for a successful build, since that state is never actually reachable on screen"`) confirming this unmount-on-success behavior is a deliberate, Playwright-verified design (the component genuinely unmounts the instant `finished` flips for a successful build) -- ruling out "just keep the screen open longer" as a viable fix, since it would contradict this already-tested, intentional design. Read `App.tsx`'s `handleBuildComplete` and confirmed it discards the entire `events` array, keeping only the final `project` -- so the only place this information could ever reach the user is through `onComplete` itself, threaded into whatever screen comes next.

**The fix**: `BuildProgress.tsx`'s effect now also computes each agent's latest event (the same `latestByAgent` logic the render body already uses) and, when some agent's latest status is still `"failed"` even though Forge succeeded, passes a plain `"<agent>: <message>"` summary as `onComplete`'s new optional second argument -- the exact real diagnostic text, matching this codebase's established "show the real message verbatim" convention (round 464's `describeMigrationHazards`, this same file's own build-summary doc comment). `App.tsx`'s `handleBuildComplete(builtProject, warning?)` stores this in a new `buildWarning` state, rendered as a `role="status"` paragraph (matching `HistoryPanel.tsx`'s `restoreWarning` pattern exactly) just under the preview screen's header -- cleared at the start of the next build (`handleBuild`), the next refine (`handleRefine`), and on logout, so it never goes stale across an unrelated later build. A genuinely recovered failure (the Debug Agent successfully retrying Database, whose LATEST event is `"success"`) is correctly NOT reported, since only a truly unrecovered latest-failed status counts.

**Tests**: added two tests to `BuildProgress.test.ts` -- one confirming `onComplete`'s second argument carries the real agent name and message for a genuine non-terminal Seed Data failure that still reaches `Forge: success`, and a negative control confirming the existing `RECOVERED_BUILD_EVENTS` fixture (a real Database failure the Debug Agent successfully fixes) produces no warning at all. Updating `onComplete`'s signature required updating two existing regex-extraction tests in `App.test.ts` that `eval` a lifted copy of `handleBuildComplete`'s body with an explicit list of injected closure parameters -- both needed a new `setBuildWarning` parameter threaded through, caught immediately as a `ReferenceError: setBuildWarning is not defined` module-load failure exactly as this codebase's own established discipline predicts. A third, previously-undiscovered regex-extraction test (`"App's handleBuild overwrites specProvider..."`) also broke the same way, since `handleBuild` now clears `buildWarning` too -- found only by running the full suite rather than just the tests touched directly, and fixed the same way.

### Round 469: round 468's own `buildWarning` state leaked across projects -- a stale non-terminal-failure notice from one project kept rendering on a completely unrelated one

**The candidate**: round 468's own trigger note flagged no known small candidate, so round 469 dispatched a genuinely fresh, unconstrained Explore survey explicitly avoiding every previously-exhausted bug shape. **Independent verification**: grepped every `setBuildWarning` call site in `App.tsx` directly and confirmed exactly 4 existed (lines 1161/1170/1206/1230 at the time, inside `handleBuild`/`handleRefine`/`handleBuildComplete`/`handleLogout`), none inside the four navigation functions named above. Read `openExistingProject` (lines 863-870) directly and confirmed it sets `view` to `"preview"` for an already-built project with no `buildWarning` reset anywhere in its body. Read `handleGoHome` (lines 1102-1115) directly -- its own existing doc comment literally describes its purpose as avoiding "a stale activeEntity/refineHistory/etc. bleeding into whatever project gets opened next," yet `buildWarning` was missing from that exact list it was written to maintain. Read `HistoryPanel`'s `onRestored` callback (lines 1958-1962) and confirmed the same gap. Confirmed the render site (the `preview` view's warning paragraph) is a single flat, unscoped `App`-level state value rendered unconditionally whenever non-null -- not scoped per-project in any way.

**The fix**: added `setBuildWarning(null)` to `openExistingProject`, `handleBackToHome`, `handleGoHome`, and `HistoryPanel`'s `onRestored` callback -- the same "clear it on every path that leaves this state behind" discipline `handleBuild`/`handleRefine`/`handleLogout` already followed, closing all four convergent leak paths this exact bug class has required before (round 461/462's "jump to record" fix, round 403's `purgeProjectPreferences` convergent-paths fix).

**Tests**: extended the existing regex-extraction tests for `openExistingProject`, `handleBackToHome`, and `handleGoHome` with a tracked `buildWarning` value seeded non-null, asserting each clears it to `null`. Added a new regression test extracting `HistoryPanel`'s inline `onRestored` callback directly out of its JSX attribute (the same "slice between JSX attributes" technique round 404's `onLeft` test established), confirming it still sets the restored project and active entity correctly while also clearing a stale `buildWarning`.

**Regression-proof**: backed up the fixed `App.tsx`, reverted it via `git checkout --` (keeping all four updated/new tests in place), confirmed all four tests failed with the exact predicted mismatch (the seeded stale warning string instead of `null`), restored from backup, confirmed byte-identical via `diff -q`, then re-ran the full `@forge/web` suite clean. Confirmed via `grep` that `apps/api/src/codegen.ts` has no duplicated copy of any of these functions (platform-only AI-build-watching UI, not part of the exported business app) -- no second copy to check.

Full suite green: **837 tests** in `@forge/web` (+1), **416 tests** in `@forge/api` (unchanged), **130 tests** in `@forge/db` (unchanged), **16 tests** in `@forge/shared` (unchanged), **109 tests** in `@forge/spec-engine` (unchanged), and a clean full monorepo `npm run build`. Commit `910a8eb`.
